rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning say as well, The world is something that ignorance causes; Why? For the Buddhas say it is so. And why then would it be wrong to say That this world is only conceptions. The meaning of this verse, according to the commentary, is that none of the many worlds that exist does so through some essence of its own: none of them are anything more than products of our conception.

query: SELECT * FROM corpus_segments WHERE course != 'C13' AND wylie LIKE ? ORDER BY course,seq
parameters: %sems gtso bo yin pa de nyid bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa%

rows.acip: ,SEMS GTZO BO YIN PA DE NYID BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA DE LA SEMS CAN GYI 'JIG RTEN NI RANG GI SEMS KYIS BSAGS PA'I LAS DANG NYON MONGS PAS BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA YIN LA, SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN SHIN TU SNA TSOGS PA NI SEMS CAN DE DAG KHO NA'I SEMS NYID KYIS BSAGS PA'I THUN MANG BA'I LAS KYIS 'GOD PA STE SKYED DE, RLUNG GI DKYIL 'KHOR NAS 'OG MIN GYI SNOD KYI MTHAR THUG PA'O,
rows.wylie: sems gtso bo yin pa de nyid bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa de la sems can gyi 'jig rten ni rang gi sems kyis bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pas bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa yin la, snod kyi 'jig rten shin tu sna tshogs pa ni sems can de dag kho na'i sems nyid kyis bsags pa'i thun mang ba'i las kyis 'god pa ste skyed de, rlung gi dkyil 'khor nas 'og min gyi snod kyi mthar thug pa'o
rows.english: The mind is the main thing; and to show this, the following explanation appears in the scripture: The world, in the form of those who live in it, finds its very being through the power of the karma they have collected with their minds, and through the bad thoughts in their minds. All the vast multitude of worlds too, in the form of the places where these beings live, have been put there, have been produced, by the collective karma of these same beings, and no one else--by the karma within their own minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

rows.acip: ,SEMS GTZO BO YIN PA DE NYID BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA DE LA SEMS CAN GYI 'JIG RTEN NI RANG GI SEMS KYIS BSAGS PA'I LAS DANG NYON MONGS PAS BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA YIN LA, SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN SHIN TU SNA TSOGS PA NI SEMS CAN DE DAG KHO NA'I SEMS NYID KYIS BSAGS PA'I THUN MANG BA'I LAS KYIS 'GOD PA STE SKYED DE, RLUNG GI DKYIL 'KHOR NAS 'OG MIN GYI SNOD KYI MTHAR THUG PA'O,
rows.wylie: sems gtso bo yin pa de nyid bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa de la sems can gyi 'jig rten ni rang gi sems kyis bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pas bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa yin la, snod kyi 'jig rten shin tu sna tshogs pa ni sems can de dag kho na'i sems nyid kyis bsags pa'i thun mang ba'i las kyis 'god pa ste skyed de, rlung gi dkyil 'khor nas 'og min gyi snod kyi mthar thug pa'o
rows.english: The mind is the main thing; and to show this, the following explanation appears in the scripture: The world, in the form of those who live in it, finds its very being through the power of the karma they have collected with their minds, and through the bad thoughts in their minds. All the vast multitude of worlds too, in the form of the places where these beings live, have been put there, have been produced, by the collective karma of these same beings, and no one else--by the karma within their own minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning say as well, The world is something that ignorance causes; Why? For the Buddhas say it is so. And why then would it be wrong to say That this world is only conceptions. The meaning of this verse, according to the commentary, is that none of the many worlds that exist does so through some essence of its own: none of them are anything more than products of our conception.

rows.english: The Buddha first turned the wheel by teaching the Four Truths of Realization three times through in twelve different aspects. From this teaching on the Four Truths alone, some disciples who belonged to the class of Listeners and whose minds were ripe grasped the meaning of dependent origination, free from the extreme of thinking of things as self-existent. It has been explained by the savior Nagarjuna in his treatises, and by Master Chandrakirti in his work on the Commentary on the Sixty Verses on Reasoning, that the scriptures of the Lower Way even describe explicitly the most subtle form of selflessness on many occasions. The second time the Buddha turned the wheel he taught in great detail about the selflessness of both the person and phenomena as is found in the brief, medium-length and extensive sutras on the Perfection of Wisdom, as well as in other works. The third time he turned the wheel he gave the teaching of the Cycle of No Return which deals extensively with the subject of method.

rows.english: We see the following sutra of the lower way quoted in A Commentary to the “Sixty Verses on Reasoning”: Anytime someone is able to eliminate every bit of this suffering; to rid themselves of it forever; to clean it away; to reach the end, free of all desire; to finish it; to put it to a final rest; to see it melt away; never to cross over into more of this suffering; never to see it come again, never to see it rise again—this then is peace, this then is beauty.

rows.acip: CES GSUNGS PA 'DIS KYANG THEG DMAN GYI MDO LAS MTHA' GNYIS BKAG PA GSUNGS PAR STON TE, MDO 'DI NI LUNG PHRAN TSEGS NA SNANG NGO, ,DE DAG KYANG MTSON PA TZAM YIN GYI, RIN CHEN PHRENG BA NA 'DIR MA DRANGS PA DU MA ZHIG DANG, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA DANG, BSTOD PA'I TSOGS LAS KYANG DU MA ZHIG GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: ces gsungs pa 'dis kyang theg dman gyi mdo las mtha' gnyis bkag pa gsungs par ston te, mdo 'di ni lung phran tshegs na snang ngo, ,de dag kyang mtshon pa tsam yin gyi, rin chen phreng ba na 'dir ma drangs pa du ma zhig dang, rigs pa drug cu pa dang, bstod pa'i tshogs las kyang du ma zhig gsungs so
rows.english: These lines are also expressing how sutras of the lower way state that both extremes should be denied—and this particular sutra citation appears in The Assorted Topics of the Word. These are all just representative examples; there are many other supporting citations from the String of Precious Jewels that we have not quoted here—as well as many others from the Sixty Verses on Reasoning, and the Collection of Praises. Refuting arguments covered in the autocommentary

rows.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I 'GREL PA LAS KYANG, MYANG 'DAS DON DAM BDEN PA DANG, BDEN PA GZHAN GSUM KUN RDZOB BDEN PAR GSUNGS TE MYANG 'DAS NI 'GOG BDEN NO,,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i 'grel pa las kyang, myang 'das don dam bden pa dang, bden pa gzhan gsum kun rdzob bden par gsungs te myang 'das ni 'gog bden no
rows.english: The commentary to the Sixty Verses on Reasoning states as well that nirvana is ultimate reality, while the other three truths are deceptive reality; and nirvana consists of the truth of the end of pain.

rows.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,'JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU, ,GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSUNGS, ,DE YI PHYIR NA 'JIG RTEN 'DI, ,RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI 'THAD,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, ,gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsungs, ,de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, ,rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad
rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning say as well: The totally enlightened Buddha Himself has stated that this world Was born from misunderstanding. Why then would it be An overstatement to say That the world is just Our imagination?

rows.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,RGYU ZAD NYID LAS ZHI BA NI, ,ZAD CES BYA BAR DMIGS PA STE,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,rgyu zad nyid las zhi ba ni, ,zad ces bya bar dmigs pa ste
rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning says, as well, We observe what we call The wearing out, Or coming to a rest, From the simple wearing out Of the cause.

rows.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG, ,'JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU, ,GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSUNG, ,DE YI PHYIR NA 'JIG RTEN 'DI, ,RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI 'THAD,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang, ,'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, ,gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsung, ,de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, ,rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad
rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning also says it like this— The total Buddhas stated That the world is rooted In misunderstanding. Why then would it ever be Incorrect to say That this entire world Is our imagination?

rows.acip: KLU SGRUB KYIS KYANG RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS, ,BRTEN NAS SKYES PAR MA SKYES PAR, ,DE NYID MKHYEN PA MCHOG GIS GSUNGS, ,ZHES DANG,
rows.wylie: klu sgrub kyis kyang rigs pa drug cu pa las, ,brten nas skyes par ma skyes par, ,de nyid mkhyen pa mchog gis gsungs, ,zhes dang
rows.english: Arya Nagarjuna has also stated, in his Sixty Verses on Reasoning: Things that start In dependence Never start— This is the very thing That the One with Highest Knowledge Has spoken.

rows.acip: ,RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I t'IKKA BZHUGS SO,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i TIkka bzhugs so
rows.english: Herein lies A Commentary to the "Sixty Verses on Reasoning." An offering of praise, and a promise

rows.acip: ,DE YI DGONGS DON MA NOR GSAL BAR STON, ,BLA MA MCHOG LA GUS PAS BTUD BYAS TE, ,RIGS PA'I DBANG PHYUG GANG GIS MDZAD PA YI, ,RIGS PA DRUG CU PA NI RNAM PAR DBYE,
rows.wylie: de yi dgongs don ma nor gsal bar ston, ,bla ma mchog la gus pas btud byas te, ,rigs pa'i dbang phyug gang gis mdzad pa yi, ,rigs pa drug cu pa ni rnam par dbye
rows.english: With reverence I bow to my Lama supreme- To the teacher who made clear, Without any error at all, That master's true intent. And so now I unravel for you The Sixty Verses on Reasoning, Composed by the Lord of Reasoning.

rows.acip: ,DE LA 'DIR BDAG NYID CHEN PO 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYIS MDZAD PA'I RIGS PA DRUG CU PA NI GANG BSHAD PAR BYA BA'I CHOS SO,,
rows.wylie: de la 'dir bdag nyid chen po 'phags pa klu sgrub kyis mdzad pa'i rigs pa drug cu pa ni gang bshad par bya ba'i chos so
rows.english: The work that I will be commenting upon in this text is the Sixty Verses on Reasoning, composed by that great being, the Realized One, Nagarjuna.

rows.acip: MTHA' GNYIS SEL BA'I RIGS PA DRUG CU PA 'DI BRTZAMS PA LAS BYUNG BA'I SGO GSUM GYI DGE BA'I RTZA BA 'DI YIS RGYU BYAS NAS, THOB PAR SHOG CIG GO
rows.wylie: mtha' gnyis sel ba'i rigs pa drug cu pa 'di brtsams pa las byung ba'i sgo gsum gyi dge ba'i rtsa ba 'di yis rgyu byas nas, thob par shog cig go
rows.english: And so a great goodness, karma of considerable power, has been accomplished here in the actions, words, and thoughts of the author, as he composed the Sixty Verses on Reasoning-which help us to clear away both extremes. And at this point, the author is dedicating this karma, that it might serve as a cause: "May they, by what I have just done, gain…"

rows.acip: *,RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I ZIN BRIS RJE'I GSUNG BZHIN RGYAL TSAB CHOS RJES BKOD PA BZHUGS SO,,
rows.wylie: *,rigs pa drug cu pa'i zin bris rje'i gsung bzhin rgyal tshab chos rjes bkod pa bzhugs so
rows.english: Herein contained are notes taken by the Dharma Lord, Gyaltsab Je, upon the occasion of a teaching granted by Lord Tsongkapa on the Sixty Verses on Reasoning.

rows.acip: RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA LA GSUM, BSTAN BCOS RTZOM PA'I SNGON 'GRO MCHOD BRJOD, BRTZAM PAR DAM BCA' BA GZHUNG DNGOS, BRTZAMS PA'I DGE BA BYANG CHUB TU BSNGO BA'O,,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa la gsum, bstan bcos rtsom pa'i sngon 'gro mchod brjod, brtsam par dam bca' ba gzhung dngos, brtsams pa'i dge ba byang chub tu bsngo ba'o
rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning covers three major topics: (1) the preliminary to composing this classical commentary, which is an offering of praise; (2) the actual text which the author has committed to compose; and (3) the dedication of the good deed of composing the text, to enlightenment.

rows.acip: DGE BA GANG LA BRTEN NAS NA, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA BRTZAMS PA'I'O,,
rows.wylie: dge ba gang la brten nas na, rigs pa drug cu pa brtsams pa'i'o
rows.english: And what good deed will be used to make this dedication? It is the merit of having composed the Sixty Verses on Reasoning.

rows.acip: ,SARBA MANGGA LAm,,
rows.wylie: sarba mangga laM
rows.english: Sarva mangalam! May goodness ever prevail! The Root Text of Arya Nagarjuna's Sixty Verses on Reasoning The Sixty Verses on Reasoning Note that for this final, combined presentation of the root text, we have used the Tengyur version of the Tibetan, as found in the Derge edition. Within Gyaltsab Je's commentary, we have retained his version of the root text, which appears to be a different translation from the Sanskrit. That translation thus has considerable value, as most of these "alternate" translations that were not included into editions of the Tengyur have been lost-and they may especially give great insight into the original Sanskrit, large portions of which are still missing for this text. For consistency, we retain the English translation of the verses from within the commentary. As described in the introduction to this volume, we have relied for the Sanskrit on the edition by Li Xuexu and Ye Shaoyong; see bibliography entry C1. Unfortunately, only portions of the original Sanskrit are still extant. Sections with major manuscript differences, such as the obeisance, are self-evident from a glance at the differing translations recorded here.

rows.acip: *,,RGYA GAR SKAD DU, YUKTI shAshtI K'A K'A RI K'A N'A MA, BOD SKAD DU, RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I TSIG LE 'UR BYAS PA ZHES BYA BA,
rows.wylie: *,,rgya gar skad du, yukti ShaShTi kA kA ri kA nA ma, bod skad du, rigs pa drug cu pa'i tshig le 'ur byas pa zhes bya ba
rows.english: In Sanskrit, this work is entitled Yukti Shashtika Karika. In the Tibetan translation, this is Rikpa Drukchupay Tsikleur Jepa. In the English translation, this is Sixty Verses on Reasoning.

rows.acip: ,RIGS PA DRUG CU PA'I TSIG LE'UR BYAS PA ZHES BYA BA SLOB DPON 'PHAGS PA KLU SGRUB KYI ZHAL SNGA NAS MDZAD PA RDZOGS SO,,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa'i tshig le'ur byas pa zhes bya ba slob dpon 'phags pa klu sgrub kyi zhal snga nas mdzad pa rdzogs so
rows.english: This concludes The Sixty Verses on Reasoning, Set in Verse, which was composed by that holy master, the Realized One, Nagarjuna.

rows.english: (verse 60) III. Arya Nagarjuna's dedication of the virtue created by this composition A Topical Listing of the Writings of Arya Nagarjuna We created this listing of the works of Arya Nagarjuna as more of a biographical exercise, than a definitive, bibliographical one. It is based primarily on three versions of the Tengyur, or collections of traditional Tibetan translations of some 3600 classical commentaries from ancient India: the Derge (widely considered the most authoritative); the Sertri ("gold calligraphy," perhaps older); and the Nartang (a solid alternative edition). We did not attempt a close analysis of additional versions of the Tengyur; and it may be that there are a few other authentic works by Arya Nagarjuna to be found there. We have not generally included works by The Arya which are reported but not actually found in these editions of the Tengyur. In some case the attribution of works to Nagarjuna is questioned by the extremely careful & competent compilers of the various Tengyurs; it was a common corruption in ancient times to say something like "my book is so good, it may as well have been written by Nagarjuna"-and then in time the book would actually be credited to him. We have studied these cases in the ancient catalogs, and we agree fully with these compilers' opinions, and have not included those particular titles. We have relied most heavily upon the truly masterful ancient native Tibetan catalog to the Derge edition. The works in the Derge Tengyur have been very admirably listed and analyzed by the creators of the great Tohoku University Catalog of this collection, and we have relied heavily upon their work. We have also availed ourselves of the fine work of Professor Lokesh Chandra in bringing the often corrupt Tibetanized Sanskrit titles into order. The number of folios in the works are patchy in the originals and may be off by one or two pages, but not more-and so they give a good idea of the relative size of each title; although of course with Arya Nagarjuna a work of 20 folios can change the history of a continent for the next 2,000 years. In some cases the same work may be referred to by different names in different editions of the Tengyur; we have tried to avoid listing both titles but a few cases may have snuck in. We have not re-created Sanskrit titles, as we consider this an inexact and potentially misleading exercise; where a title is not mentioned in situ, we have noted that fact. The translations of the titles into English is by the two translators of the present volume. We have broken the titles down into subject categories, according to our judgement and a quick review of the contents of works. In ordering them, we generally follow the lead of the native creators of the Derge Tengyur. These categories may perhaps be polished in time, but for now are very indicative of topics that The Arya considered important; which is the purpose of the exercise for our present volume. rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang , 'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, , gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsungs, , de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, , rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad, , ces gsungs pa'i don 'grel par 'jig rten rnams rang gi ngo bos ma grub pa rtog pas btags pa tsam du bshad cing
rows.english: The Sixty Verses on Reasoning say as well, The world is something that ignorance causes; Why? For the Buddhas say it is so. And why then would it be wrong to say That this world is only conceptions. The meaning of this verse, according to the commentary, is that none of the many worlds that exist does so through some essence of its own: none of them are anything more than products of our conception.

rows.english: Now the Sixty Verses on Reasoning says, The world is something that ignorance causes; Why? For the Buddhas say it is so. And why then would it be wrong to say That this world is only conceptions. If one were to end his ignorance, Then how is it that the thing that's ended, Despite our misunderstanding, could never Disappear, even in conceptions?

rows.english: But your example does not hold true. A lamp is not something which illuminates itself, because it is not something which is the object illuminated by it. There is no need for it to illuminate itself, and it could never do so anyway. If it could, then darkness too shroud both itself and other objects. This though could never be, for the reason that there is no such thing as darkness shrouding darkness. If it did shroud darkness, then it would be like shrouding a vase with a piece of cloth, and we would be unable to see the darkness itself. For these points I am enlarging upon statements found in the Root Text on Wisdom [by the realized being Nagarjuna].

rows.acip: ,DE BZHIN DU PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS NGA'O SNYAM PA 'BYUNG BA NA, PHUNG PO'I STENG NAS SNGA PHYI'I RGYUN GYI TSOGS PA DANG , DUS GCIG PA'I TSOGS PA DANG DE'I CHA SHAS DE'I MTSAN GZHIR 'JOG RGYU CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DE RGYAS PAR 'OG NAS 'CHAD DE,
rows.wylie: de bzhin du phung po la brten nas nga'o snyam pa 'byung ba na, phung po'i steng nas snga phyi'i rgyun gyi tshogs pa dang , dus gcig pa'i tshogs pa dang de'i cha shas de'i mtshan gzhir 'jog rgyu cung zad kyang med de rgyas par 'og nas 'chad de
rows.english: The same thing happens when you get the idea of "me" about the heaps, the various components to yourself. There is nothing about these components as a whole, when you consider them as a continuum in time, nor as a whole considered in a single moment in time, nor as the various parts to a whole, that you could ever establish as being any kind of "me." We'll go into this in more detail further on.

rows.acip: ,DE'I PHYIR DANG PHUNG PO'I CHA DANG CHA CAN LAS NGO BO THA DAD PA'I DE'I GZHIR 'DZIN RGYU YANG CUNG ZAD KYANG MED PAS, NGA DE NI RTOG PAS PHUNG PO LA BRTEN NAS BZHAG PA TZAM YIN GYI, RANG GI NGO BOS GRUB PA MED DO,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir dang phung po'i cha dang cha can las ngo bo tha dad pa'i de'i gzhir 'dzin rgyu yang cung zad kyang med pas, nga de ni rtog pas phung po la brten nas bzhag pa tsam yin gyi, rang gi ngo bos grub pa med do
rows.english: Because of this fact, and since moreover there is not the slightest thing outside of the parts or whole of the components to yourself that you could ever consider any kind of "me," this "me" is nothing more than a creation of conception, based on the components. There is no "me" which exists through any essence of its own. ********* Selection Five: What the Buddha really meant when He said that things were "mind only"

rows.acip: ,RIGS PA DRUG CU PA LAS KYANG , 'JIG RTEN MA RIG RKYEN CAN DU, , GANG PHYIR RDZOGS PA'I SANGS RGYAS GSUNG , , DE YI PHYIR NA 'JIG RTEN 'DI, , RNAM RTOG YIN ZHES CIS MI 'THAD, , MA RIG 'GAGS PAR GYUR NA NI, , GANG ZHIG 'GAG PAR 'GYUR BA DE, , MI SHES PA LAS KUN BRTAGS PAR, , JI LTA BUR NA GSAL MI 'GYUR, , ZHES GSUNGS TE,
rows.wylie: rigs pa drug cu pa las kyang , 'jig rten ma rig rkyen can du, , gang phyir rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas gsung , , de yi phyir na 'jig rten 'di, , rnam rtog yin zhes cis mi 'thad, , ma rig 'gags par gyur na ni, , gang zhig 'gag par 'gyur ba de, , mi shes pa las kun brtags par, , ji lta bur na gsal mi 'gyur, , zhes gsungs te
rows.english: Now the Sixty Verses on Reasoning says, The world is something that ignorance causes; Why? For the Buddhas say it is so. And why then would it be wrong to say That this world is only conceptions. If one were to end his ignorance, Then how is it that the thing that's ended, Despite our misunderstanding, could never Disappear, even in conceptions?

rows.acip: RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PAR 'GYUR LA, DE'I TSE 'KHRUL PA LOG PA NA GSAL DU 'GRO DGOS KYI, LDOG PAR MI 'GYUR RO, , ZHES PA'I DON NO,
rows.wylie: rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na gnas lugs su grub par 'gyur la, de'i tshe 'khrul pa log pa na gsal du 'gro dgos kyi, ldog par mi 'gyur ro, , zhes pa'i don no
rows.english: The meaning of the lines is as follows. If things existed in their very essence, then they would exist as some independent reality. If this were so, then when you finally stopped your mistaken states of mind, they would never disappear, although they should have.

rows.acip: ,SEMS GTZO BO YIN PA DE NYID BSTAN PA'I PHYIR BSHAD PA DE LA SEMS CAN GYI 'JIG RTEN NI RANG GI SEMS KYIS BSAGS PA'I LAS DANG NYON MONGS PAS BDAG GI DNGOS PO RNYED PA YIN LA, SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN SHIN TU SNA TSOGS PA NI SEMS CAN DE DAG KHO NA'I SEMS NYID KYIS BSAGS PA'I THUN MANG BA'I LAS KYIS 'GOD PA STE SKYED DE, RLUNG GI DKYIL 'KHOR NAS 'OG MIN GYI SNOD KYI MTHAR THUG PA'O,
rows.wylie: sems gtso bo yin pa de nyid bstan pa'i phyir bshad pa de la sems can gyi 'jig rten ni rang gi sems kyis bsags pa'i las dang nyon mongs pas bdag gi dngos po rnyed pa yin la, snod kyi 'jig rten shin tu sna tshogs pa ni sems can de dag kho na'i sems nyid kyis bsags pa'i thun mang ba'i las kyis 'god pa ste skyed de, rlung gi dkyil 'khor nas 'og min gyi snod kyi mthar thug pa'o
rows.english: The mind is the main thing; and to show this, the following explanation appears in the scripture: The world, in the form of those who live in it, finds its very being through the power of the karma they have collected with their minds, and through the bad thoughts in their minds. All the vast multitude of worlds too, in the form of the places where these beings live, have been put there, have been produced, by the collective karma of these same beings, and no one else--by the karma within their own minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

rows.acip: ,DE LA RMA BYA LA SOGS PA'I MDONGS LA SOGS PA SNA TSOGS PA NI, SEMS CAN DE RNAMS KHO NA'I LAS THUN MONG MA YIN PAS SKYED PA'O, , PAD MA LA SOGS PA'I 'DAB MA DANG KHA DOG SNA TSOGS PA NI, SEMS CAN GYI THUN MONG GI LAS KYIS BSKYED PA'O, , DE BZHIN DU GZHAN LA'ANG SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: de la rma bya la sogs pa'i mdongs la sogs pa sna tshogs pa ni, sems can de rnams kho na'i las thun mong ma yin pas skyed pa'o, , pad ma la sogs pa'i 'dab ma dang kha dog sna tshogs pa ni, sems can gyi thun mong gi las kyis bskyed pa'o, , de bzhin du gzhan la'ang shes par bya'o
rows.english: On this subject, the intricate patterns on a peacock and other such objects are produced by each one's personal karma. The intricacies of the petals and colors of a lotus flower and other such things are produced by the collective karma of living beings. You can apply these principles to all other cases as well.

rows.acip: ,JI SKAD DU, SEMS CAN LAS KYI DBANG GIS RI, , NAG PO'I DUS SU SKYES TE DPER, , SEMS DMYAL MTHO RIS 'JIG RTEN DU, , MTSON DANG RIN CHEN SHING BZHIN NO, , ZHES GSUNGS SO, , 'JIG RTEN GNYIS THUN MONG GI LAS YIN MIN GNYIS KYIS BSKYED PA NI, SEMS TZAM GYI GZHUNG DU YANG BSHAD PAS SEMS TZAM GYI LUGS LA'ANG SNOD KYI 'JIG RTEN MED PA MIN NO,
rows.wylie: ji skad du, sems can las kyi dbang gis ri, , nag po'i dus su skyes te dper, , sems dmyal mtho ris 'jig rten du, , mtshon dang rin chen shing bzhin no, , zhes gsungs so, , 'jig rten gnyis thun mong gi las yin min gnyis kyis bskyed pa ni, sems tsam gyi gzhung du yang bshad pas sems tsam gyi lugs la'ang snod kyi 'jig rten med pa min no
rows.english: As the verse goes, It's through the karma of living beings That the great dark mountains arise in their time. It's like the hells, and the heavens above, And swords, and jewels, and trees in the world. The great books of the Mind-Only School also discuss whether the two worlds [of beings and the place they live] are produced by karma that is collective or not, and so it's not as though the system of the Mind Only denies the existence of the world where beings live.

rows.english: None of these things that seem to be pleasure though is pleasure by nature, or pleasure in its very essence. If they were, then you would feel more pleasant the more you had of them. But this is not the case, for as you get more and more of them they too start to give you pain. When this happens we can understand that they are not pleasure by nature. They are, in fact, suffering--they are what we call the "suffering of change."

rows.english: "What," you may ask, "is the very essence of this morality?" To put it briefly, it has four wonderful qualities: 1) The morality is accepted from others, in an excellent way; and 2) The motivation for taking it on is extremely pure. 3) If one fails in the morality, one can recover; and 4) One can develop a sense of reverence for the morality, maintain then a sense of recollection, and thus prevent oneself from failing.

rows.acip: GSUM PA NI, KUN BRTAGS MTSAN NYID NGO BO NYID MED PA YIN NA KUN BRTAGS NYID GANG YIN SNYAM NA, DE NI DGONGS 'GREL LAS, RNAM PAR RTOG PA'I SPYOD YUL KUN BRTAGS PA'I MTSAN NYID KYI GNAS 'DU BYED KYI MTSAN MA LA GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO ZHES NGO BO NYID DAM BYE BRAG GI MTSAN NYID DU MING DANG BRDAR RNAM PAR BZHAG PA DANG , GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO SKYE'O ZHE'AM 'GAG PA ZHE'AM GZUGS KYI PHUNG PO SPANG BA DANG YONGS SU SHES PA ZHES NGO BO NYID KYI MTSAN NYID DAM BYE BRAG GI MTSAN NYID DU MING DANG BRDAS RNAM PAR BZHAG PA GANG LAGS PA DE NI KUN BRTAGS PA'I MTSAN NYID LAGS TE, ZHES GSUNGS SO, ,
rows.wylie: gsum pa ni, kun brtags mtshan nyid ngo bo nyid med pa yin na kun brtags nyid gang yin snyam na, de ni dgongs 'grel las, rnam par rtog pa'i spyod yul kun brtags pa'i mtshan nyid kyi gnas 'du byed kyi mtshan ma la gzugs kyi phung po zhes ngo bo nyid dam bye brag gi mtshan nyid du ming dang brdar rnam par bzhag pa dang , gzugs kyi phung po skye'o zhe'am 'gag pa zhe'am gzugs kyi phung po spang ba dang yongs su shes pa zhes ngo bo nyid kyi mtshan nyid dam bye brag gi mtshan nyid du ming dang brdas rnam par bzhag pa gang lags pa de ni kun brtags pa'i mtshan nyid lags te, zhes gsungs so,
rows.english: Here is the third division from above: an identification of the nature of the three real natures. "You have said," one may begin, "that the 'lack of a definitive nature' refers to constructs. But just what are these constructs themselves?" Our answer is drawn from the Commentary on the True Intent: Consider that thing which is established through names and terms as either the attribute that relates to the very essence, or the attribute that relates to some particular, when we focus on something which is (1) the arena in which the constructing state of mind acts; (2) the object of the attribute of constructs; and (3) that which exhibits the typical features of a factor; and speak of it as "the heap of physical matter." Consider as well that thing which is established through names and terms as either the attribute that relates to the very essence, or the attribute that relates to some particular, when we focus on the same thing and speak of "the growing of the heap of physical matter," or its "stopping," or "eliminating" or "grasping" this heap of physical matter. This thing is what we refer to as "the attribute of constructs."

rows.acip: SDUG BDEN LA NI GDAGS GZHI SNGAR BZHIN LA SDUG BSNGAL GYI BDEN PA'O ZHES NGO BO DANG SDUG BDEN YONGS SU SHES PA ZHES BYE BRAG TU MING DANG BRDAS BZHAG PA KUN BRTAGS DANG , GZHAN DBANG SNGAR BZHIN DANG YONGS GRUB KYANG SNGAR DANG 'DRA LA NGO BO NYID DE KHO NAS NGO BO NYID MA MCHIS PA ZHES GSUNGS SHING , DE BZHIN DU BDEN PA LHAG MA LA YANG SBYAR RO, ,
rows.wylie: sdug bden la ni gdags gzhi sngar bzhin la sdug bsngal gyi bden pa'o zhes ngo bo dang sdug bden yongs su shes pa zhes bye brag tu ming dang brdas bzhag pa kun brtags dang , gzhan dbang sngar bzhin dang yongs grub kyang sngar dang 'dra la ngo bo nyid de kho nas ngo bo nyid ma mchis pa zhes gsungs shing , de bzhin du bden pa lhag ma la yang sbyar ro,
rows.english: Let's take for example the truth of suffering. The constructs here are those things that are established through names and terms when you focus on the object of your construct and think to yourself either of its very essence--with the words "truth of suffering"--or of its particulars, in wording such as "The truth of suffering is something that a person should realize is happening to them." The dependent thing here is just the same as we described it above, and so is the totality; you can even use the same expression and say it is "impossible for it to have any nature of having that one specific nature." Use this same pattern for the other truths.

rows.english: If we go further and investigate just what the mind itself is, we realize that it is empty. That is, if we look everywhere to try to find the very essence of the mind that is doing the thinking, we realize that it is empty. And when we do thus come to that realization, we are engaging in what's called the “deep practice free of signs.”

rows.english: That is, when we are coming to understand the very essence of all things, it is not the case that we come to understand that what is there is some absence of everything.

rows.acip: GANG GI TSE BAR SKABS SU SEMS PHYI ROL DU RNAM PAR G-YENGS PAR MTHONG BA DE'I TSE DE'I NGO BO NYID LA BRTAGS NAS RNAM PAR G-YENGS PA ZHI BAR BYAS LA YANG DE NYID DU SEMS GZHAG PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: gang gi tshe bar skabs su sems phyi rol du rnam par g-yengs par mthong ba de'i tshe de'i ngo bo nyid la brtags nas rnam par g-yengs pa zhi bar byas la yang de nyid du sems gzhag par bya'o
rows.english: In the event that there are intervals where you see that your mind is being distracted to the outside, you can simply use that itself as an object of your investigation into the very essence of things, and thus bring the distraction to a stop. And then you place the mind back on suchness, once again. Learning to take breaks

rows.acip: ,BRGYAD PA KUN GZHI RNAM SHES LA YANG NGO BO NYID KYI KUN GZHI ZHES SANGS RGYAS 'GRUB PA'I DON DANG LDAN PA ZHIG DANG, RNAM SMIN GYI KUN GZHI ZHES KHAMS BCO BRGYAD LA DMIGS PA ZHIG DANG, KUN NAS NYON MONGS PA'I KUN GZHI ZHES CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN ZHIG STE, GSUM DU 'CHAD PA DANG,
rows.wylie: brgyad pa kun gzhi rnam shes la yang ngo bo nyid kyi kun gzhi zhes sangs rgyas 'grub pa'i don dang ldan pa zhig dang, rnam smin gyi kun gzhi zhes khams bco brgyad la dmigs pa zhig dang, kun nas nyon mongs pa'i kun gzhi zhes chos kyi bdag 'dzin zhig ste, gsum du 'chad pa dang
rows.english: Master Paramartha then explains [8] the eighth type of consciousness—foundation consciousness—by dividing it further into three different kinds.  The first he calls “the foundation consciousness of the very essence,” referring to a foundation consciousness which contains the very point of attaining enlightenment.  Second is “foundation consciousness as a ripening,” which is a form of this consciousness that is focused upon the eighteen categories.  And third comes “foundation consciousness for total negativity,” which is another particular kind of grasping to self-existence: one which holds to the self-existence of things.

rows.acip: 'O NA GANG ZHIG YANG DANG YANG DU YUL GYI NGO BO NYID DU MDUN DU SNANG BAR MTHONG BA DE, CI ZHIG TU 'GYUR BAR 'OS SHE NA,
rows.wylie: 'o na gang zhig yang dang yang du yul gyi ngo bo nyid du mdun du snang bar mthong ba de, ci zhig tu 'gyur bar 'os she na
rows.english: Which would lead one then to the following question: Well then, but it does happen that there is something which makes its appearance before us, over and over, as the very essence of an object of perception; and we observe it. How then would that ever be something that could happen?

rows.acip: SKAD CIG SNGA PHYI BA RNAMS NGO BO NYID KYIS GZHAN YIN NA, DE'I TSE BYED PA PO'I BDAG MED PAS, LAS LA YANG GNAS PA'I RTEN MED PA'I PHYIR LAS KYANG MED PAS, LAS DE'I 'BRAS BU DANG 'BREL BA MED PA NYID DU 'GYUR RO,,
rows.wylie: skad cig snga phyi ba rnams ngo bo nyid kyis gzhan yin na, de'i tshe byed pa po'i bdag med pas, las la yang gnas pa'i rten med pa'i phyir las kyang med pas, las de'i 'bras bu dang 'brel ba med pa nyid du 'gyur ro
rows.english: Suppose then that successive moments, previous and subsequent, were other than each other, by their very essence. In that case, there could be no self to the agent involved; and so there would moreover be no basis for the action itself to remain—which means there would be no action either. And then there would be absolutely no connection to the result of such an action.

rows.acip: SIL SNYAN DE DAG LAS DNGOS PO MED PA'I NGO BO NYID KYI SGRA DANG, THEG PA CHEN PO'I GTAM GYI SGRA 'BYUNG BA, SGRA DE THOS PAS SEMS CAN THAMS CAD SANGS RGYAS KYI BYANG CHUB LAS PHYIR MI LDOG PAR 'GYUR BA'O,,
rows.wylie: sil snyan de dag las dngos po med pa'i ngo bo nyid kyi sgra dang, theg pa chen po'i gtam gyi sgra 'byung ba, sgra de thos pas sems can thams cad sangs rgyas kyi byang chub las phyir mi ldog par 'gyur ba'o
rows.english: Those cymbals release a roar which speaks itself of the very essence of things—of the way these things are not themselves.  The sounds relate the story of the greater way; and every being who hears them reaches a point where they are unstoppable in their progress towards enlightenment.

rows.acip: DRIL BU G-YER KA'I DRA BA DE DAG KYANG RLUNG GIS BSKYOD CING BSKUL BA NA LHA'I SGRA DBYANGS YID DU 'ONG BA SEMS CAN THAMS CAD YANG DAG PAR DGA' BAR BYED PA, DNGOS PO MED PA'I NGO BO NYID KYI CHOS KYI SGRA SKAD 'BYUNG BA,
rows.wylie: dril bu g-yer ka'i dra ba de dag kyang rlung gis bskyod cing bskul ba na lha'i sgra dbyangs yid du 'ong ba sems can thams cad yang dag par dga' bar byed pa, dngos po med pa'i ngo bo nyid kyi chos kyi sgra skad 'byung ba
rows.english: When breezes come through and inspire the bells with a nudge, they ring out with a lovely song of the gods, filling the beings who hear it with pure joy.  So too these sounds speak of the very essence of things—of the way that things are not themselves.

rows.acip: RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PAR 'GYUR LA DE'I TSE 'KHRUL, PA LOG PA NA GSAL DU 'GRO DGOS KYI LDOG PAR MI 'GYUR RO ZHES PA'I DON NO
rows.wylie: rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na gnas lugs su grub par 'gyur la de'i tshe 'khrul, pa log pa na gsal du 'gro dgos kyi ldog par mi 'gyur ro zhes pa'i don no
rows.english: The meaning of the lines is as follows. If things existed in their very essence, then they would exist as some independent reality. If this were so, then when you finally stopped your mistaken states of mind, they would never disappear,

rows.acip: NGO BO NYID MED TSUL NI, NGO BOS MED CES PAS STON TE, GANG ZAG DANG GZUGS LA SOGS PA'I CHOS LA NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN MED CES PA'O, ,BSHAD PA DE DAG NI GRUB CHEN MTSO SKYES KYI 'GREL PA'I DGONGS PA'O, ,'DI NI RANG BZHIN GYIS DANG RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS MED CES GSUNG RAB LAS MANG DU 'BYUNG BA RNAMS KYI DON NO,,
rows.wylie: ngo bo nyid med tshul ni, ngo bos med ces pas ston te, gang zag dang gzugs la sogs pa'i chos la ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin med ces pa'o, ,bshad pa de dag ni grub chen mtsho skyes kyi 'grel pa'i dgongs pa'o, ,'di ni rang bzhin gyis dang rang gi mtshan nyid kyis med ces gsung rab las mang du 'byung ba rnams kyi don no
rows.english: The way in which these things lack any essence of their own is indicated in the words "nothing which exists in its very essence."  That is to say, "No objects--neither the person nor the things that make up a person (such as their physical form)--have any kind of nature where they exist through some very essence of their own."  The explanation of the lines we have given here represents the ideas expressed by the great and accomplished master Saroruha in his commentary.  The same point is being made many times throughout the teachings of the highest word when they say that "nothing has any nature of its own," or "nothing exists by definition."

rows.acip: SHES RAB CAN GANG DAG GANG ZAG DANG CHOS KYI NGO BO RNAMS, RANG RANG GI RGYU DANG RKYEN LA BRTEN NAS 'BYUNG BA DANG, BRTEN NAS BTAGS PA YIN PA'I PHYIR NA, BDEN PA DANG YANG DAG PAR MED DO, ,ZHES 'DI DAG LA RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB PA'I RANG BZHIN CUNG ZAD KYANG MED DE,
rows.wylie: shes rab can gang dag gang zag dang chos kyi ngo bo rnams, rang rang gi rgyu dang rkyen la brten nas 'byung ba dang, brten nas btags pa yin pa'i phyir na, bden pa dang yang dag par med do, ,zhes 'di dag la rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub pa'i rang bzhin cung zad kyang med de
rows.english: What this is saying is that those of wisdom grasp the following.  The very essence of all things--whether they relate to the person or to the things that make up a person--is that they occur through dependence on their particular causes and conditions: they are projections based on something else.  As such they do not exist as something which is real or "pure."  They possess not even the slightest bit of any nature which could ever exist in and of itself.

rows.acip: DE'I DAM TSIG GSUNGS PA YIN TE, RDO RJE SKU GSUNG LA GNAS PA, ZHES BYA BA NI, ,RNAM PAR SNANG MDZAD LA SOGS PA'I RDO RJE GSUM GYI NGO BO NYID DO,,
rows.wylie: de'i dam tshig gsungs pa yin te, rdo rje sku gsung la gnas pa, zhes bya ba ni, ,rnam par snang mdzad la sogs pa'i rdo rje gsum gyi ngo bo nyid do
rows.english: What's being described is our pledge towards Her.  The statement that "She resides in the Diamond body, speech, and mind" is meant to indicate that She is, in Her very essence, the three enlightened diamonds of the Angel of Various Appearances, and the rest.

rows.acip: DE LA DBANG PO RAB KYI RAB CHAGS SOGS KYI NYES PA MI SPYOD PA RNAM RTOG SHAS CHUNG BA SNYING RJE CHE BA GNYIS MED KYI DE KHO NA NYID LA BRTZON PA LA, SNYING RJE CHEN PO DANG RO GCIG PA CHOS BDAG MED PA'I YE SHES KYI NGO BO NYID MING GZHAN THABS SHES ZHES BYA BA'I PHYAG CHEN STON TO,,
rows.wylie: de la dbang po rab kyi rab chags sogs kyi nyes pa mi spyod pa rnam rtog shas chung ba snying rje che ba gnyis med kyi de kho na nyid la brtson pa la, snying rje chen po dang ro gcig pa chos bdag med pa'i ye shes kyi ngo bo nyid ming gzhan thabs shes zhes bya ba'i phyag chen ston to
rows.english: Now for those whose faculties are the best of the best--for those who have none of the problems of attachment and so on in the way they behave; who have but few wrong ideas; who possess great compassion; and who make great efforts in the suchness of the indivisible--teach them the Great Seal, that which is a single song with great compassion, the very essence of the wisdom of no-self-nature, also known as method and wisdom.

rows.acip: RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA (STE, CHOS RNAMS KYI YIN LUGS KYI) 'I NGO BO NYID SHES PA (DES MTSAN 'DZIN GYI RTOG PA 'JOMS PAS NI), SANGS RGYAS NYID DE RDO RJE 'CHANG CHEN PO NYID 'GRUB PAR 'GYUR ZHING (STE, GO 'PHANG DER), BDAG NYID RDZOGS PAR 'GYUR BA STE, DRANG BA'I DON TO,,
rows.wylie: rnam par mi rtog pa (ste, chos rnams kyi yin lugs kyi) 'i ngo bo nyid shes pa (des mtshan 'dzin gyi rtog pa 'joms pas ni), sangs rgyas nyid de rdo rje 'chang chen po nyid 'grub par 'gyur zhing (ste, go 'phang der), bdag nyid rdzogs par 'gyur ba ste, drang ba'i don to
rows.english: A practitioner like this, who no longer misperceives things, understands the very essence of things--(which is to say, the true nature of these things).  (And with this understanding, they are able to destroy their tendency to misperceive things, seeing them as existing in their indications.)  And then they will attain no less than Buddhahood: the state of the great Keeper of the Diamond.  And (in this state) they will come to the perfection of their very being--itself a term which is figurative. * Partner Practice and the Ordained Are ordained people allowed to engage in practice with an actual, physical partner?  For an answer, we turn first to Choney Lama's Cloud of Offerings to Please the Great Lord Atisha: Brief Words of Clarity in Explanation of the 'Lamp on the Path to Enlightenment' (ACIP uncataloged data, ff. 19b-20b).  The Lama is discussing the propriety of partner practice with reference to the tantric empowerment of the ordained (here referred to as "those who follow the path of celibacy").

rows.acip: DE LTA BU'I BLA MA'I NGO BO GANG ZHE NA, SPYIR MCHOG DMAN JI LTAR YIN YANG, 'DIR MOS PA LA BLTOS NAS BLA MA DE NI (SANGS RGYAS KUN GYI NGO BO NYID) DE BDAG NYID CAN NO,,
rows.wylie: de lta bu'i bla ma'i ngo bo gang zhe na, spyir mchog dman ji ltar yin yang, 'dir mos pa la bltos nas bla ma de ni (sangs rgyas kun gyi ngo bo nyid) de bdag nyid can no
rows.english: "What," you may ask, "is the very essence of such a Lama?"  Regardless of how you happen to perceive your Lama--as someone ultimately high, or somewhat lower--we are here thinking of Them as someone who is the essence of all the Buddhas, meaning a single person who combines all these Buddhas within Them. Picturing Our Lama as the Emanation of a Buddha

rows.acip: DES NA SEMS CAN GYI BLO DON MTHUN GYIS GANG BZHAG THAMS CAD KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA ZHES BYA BA YIN TE, KUN RDZOB BDEN 'DZIN DE NYID THOG MA MED PA'I BAG CHAGS 'KHRUL PA'I DBANG GIS BYUNG ZHING , DES KYANG SROG CHAGS THAMS CAD LA GZUGS SOGS KYI CHOS RNAMS YANG DAG PAR DNGOS PO'I BDAG NYID DU GRUB PA LTA BUR NYE BAR BSTAN PA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR BA DE'I PHYIR GZUGS SOGS KYI DNGOS PO RNAMS YANG DAG PAR MA GRUB PA LA DE LAS BZLOG STE, YANG DAG PAR GRUB PAR 'DZIN PA'I BLO GANG YIN PA DE NI KUN RDZOB CES BYA BA YIN TE, RANG NYID DNGOS PO'I GNAS LUGS MTHONG BA LA RMONGS PA DANG , GZHAN GYI DNGOS PO'I DE KHO NA NYID MTHONG BA LA SGRIBS PA LTA BUR BYED, 'GEBS PA LTA BUR BYED PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: des na sems can gyi blo don mthun gyis gang bzhag thams cad kun rdzob tu yod pa zhes bya ba yin te, kun rdzob bden 'dzin de nyid thog ma med pa'i bag chags 'khrul pa'i dbang gis byung zhing , des kyang srog chags thams cad la gzugs sogs kyi chos rnams yang dag par dngos po'i bdag nyid du grub pa lta bur nye bar bstan pa mthong bar 'gyur ba de'i phyir gzugs sogs kyi dngos po rnams yang dag par ma grub pa la de las bzlog ste, yang dag par grub par 'dzin pa'i blo gang yin pa de ni kun rdzob ces bya ba yin te, rang nyid dngos po'i gnas lugs mthong ba la rmongs pa dang , gzhan gyi dngos po'i de kho na nyid mthong ba la sgribs pa lta bur byed, 'gebs pa lta bur byed pa'i phyir
rows.english: Therefore any and every object whose existence is established by a consistent state of mind belonging to a living being who is not a Buddha is said to exist "deceptively." The deceptive state of mind occurs by force of a deep mental seed which causes it to be mistaken; this is a seed for the tendency to grasp to things as being real, and it has been in our minds for time without beginning. This seed makes every living creature who is not a Buddha see every existing phenomenon, physical form and the rest, look as if it were a pure, discrete entity. And so we call a state of mind "deceptive" when it holds that physical form and all other things purely exist, whereas in fact they are quite the opposite: they do not purely exist. We say it is "deceptive" [Sanskrit: saw^ vr

rows.acip: ,'O NA MTHONG LAM BAR CHAD MED LAM GYI DUS SU DE'I SPANG BYA MTHONG SPANG MED MOD KYANG , SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL YOD DGOS LA, DE'I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA'I ZAG MED YIN PAS, DE'I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA, DBANG SHES KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA KUN GZHI YANG MI 'DOD PAS DE'I RTEN MED PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM NA, SKYON MED DE DE'I TSE NGA TZAM ZHIG SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL GYI RTEN YIN PA'I PHYIR TE, SPANG GNYEN GZHAN LA YANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: 'o na mthong lam bar chad med lam gyi dus su de'i spang bya mthong spang med mod kyang , sgom spang gi bag la nyal yod dgos la, de'i tshe yid kyi shes pa ni gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i zag med yin pas, de'i ngo bor bag la nyal de gnas pa mi rigs la, dbang shes kyang de'i rten du med cing gzugs kyang de'i rten du mi rigs la kun gzhi yang mi 'dod pas de'i rten med par 'gyur ro snyam na, skyon med de de'i tshe nga tsam zhig sgom spang gi bag la nyal gyi rten yin pa'i phyir te, spang gnyen gzhan la yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o
rows.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things could stay. And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. ********* Selection Three: The Middle-Way School on the question of where the seeds of karma stay until they give their resu

rows.english: The meaning of the lines is as follows. If things existed in their very essence, then they would exist as some independent reality. If this were so, then when you finally stopped your mistaken states of mind, they would never disappear, although they should have.
