rows.english: Here is the third point. The person who was mistaken--that is, I myself--confess whatever harm I may ever have done towards the Three Jewels, or towards my parents, and towards any other such high object of merit; I confess all these actions, which were caused by the mental afflictions known as the three poisons, and which were expressed with either my bodily actions, my speech, and my thoughts.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, GAL TE CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MED NA SGYU MA 'DZIN PA'I SHES PA 'KHRUL PA'ANG YOD PA MIN NA SGYU MA BLO GANG GIS DMIGS PAR 'GYUR TE, MI 'GYUR BAS SGYU MA'ANG MED PAR 'GYUR RO ZHE NA 'DI YANG YOD NA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD DGOS SNYAM PA'I RTZOD PA'O,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, gal te chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis med na sgyu ma 'dzin pa'i shes pa 'khrul pa'ang yod pa min na sgyu ma blo gang gis dmigs par 'gyur te, mi 'gyur bas sgyu ma'ang med par 'gyur ro zhe na 'di yang yod na rang bzhin gyis yod dgos snyam pa'i rtsod pa'o
rows.english: Here is the first of the two. One may begin with the following objection: If there is no object at all that has any nature of its own, then the mistaken state of mind which perceives the illusion cannot exist either. If this were so, then there would be no state of mind that could ever take the illusion as its object. And if this were the case, then the illusion itself could not exist either. This argument too is another version of the idea that, if something exists, it must have a nature of its own.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR KHA CIG GIS MDO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS DUS GSUM PAR GSUNGS PA'I MDO THAMS CAD NGES DON DU BSGRUBS NAS GZHAN SDE'I RIGS CAN BDAG TU SMRA BA LA ZHEN PA RNAMS DRANG BA'I PHYIR DU GSUNGS PA 'GA' ZHIG SGRA JI BZHIN PAR 'DOD CING , CHOS NYID MA GTOGS PA'I CHOS CAN THAMS CAD 'KHRUL PA'I BLOS RLOM PA MA GTOGS PA RANG GI NGO BO GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED CING CHOS NYID BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I BDEN MI BDEN RNAM PAR PHYE BA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA'I LEGS PAR RNAM PAR PHYE BA'I DON DU 'DOD DO, ,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir kha cig gis mdo 'di la brten nas dus gsum par gsungs pa'i mdo thams cad nges don du bsgrubs nas gzhan sde'i rigs can bdag tu smra ba la zhen pa rnams drang ba'i phyir du gsungs pa 'ga' zhig sgra ji bzhin par 'dod cing , chos nyid ma gtogs pa'i chos can thams cad 'khrul pa'i blos rlom pa ma gtogs pa rang gi ngo bo grub pa cung zad kyang med cing chos nyid bden par grub pa'i bden mi bden rnam par phye ba ni sngar bshad pa'i legs par rnam par phye ba'i don du 'dod do,
rows.english: Given all this, some have used the wording of this sutra to go on and claim that it proves that everything which Lord Buddha taught during all the periods is meant to be taken literally. These people would then have to say that certain statements which the Buddha made to attract those of other religions who still believed that things could have some self-nature are teachings that we are meant to take on face value. They also say that no object but the real nature of things is anything more than the simple delusion of a mistaken state of mind; these other things have not the slightest bit of an existing nature to them. They say finally that the meaning of "fine distinctions" is the distinction between what exists in truth or not, in the sense of being this one true thing: the real nature of things.

rows.acip: DES NA GZHAN DBANG GI SKYE 'GAG BLO 'KHRUL PAS SKYE 'GAG TU ZHEN PA TZAM GYI NGOR YIN PAS KUN RDZOB TU SKYE 'GAG YOD PAS SKUR 'DEBS SU MI 'GYUR RO ZHES PAS LAN MI THEBS TE,
rows.wylie: des na gzhan dbang gi skye 'gag blo 'khrul pas skye 'gag tu zhen pa tsam gyi ngor yin pas kun rdzob tu skye 'gag yod pas skur 'debs su mi 'gyur ro zhes pas lan mi thebs te
rows.english: Don't respond to us then by saying that--since the growing and stopping of dependent things is only something that exists to a mistaken state of mind which is imagining that things are growing and stopping--growing and stopping are things that exist, in a deceptive way; and that therefore there is no discounting of these things occurring here.

rows.acip: GAL TE DE LTAR DMIGS PA'I BLOS MI GNOD DE BLO DE NYID 'KHRUL PA'I DNGOS PO YIN PA'I PHYIR RO, , ZHE NA,
rows.wylie: gal te de ltar dmigs pa'i blos mi gnod de blo de nyid 'khrul pa'i dngos po yin pa'i phyir ro, , zhe na
rows.english: And suppose you say that "our position is not disproved by a state of mind which sees things this way, for it is itself a mistaken thing."

rows.acip: 'O NA 'KHRUL PA DE RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS YOD NA NI NGO BO NYID MED PA DON DAM DU MI RUNG LA, MED NA NI 'KHRUL PA'I PHYIR DMIGS KYANG MED DO, , ZHES PA DE MI 'THAD DO, ,
rows.wylie: 'o na 'khrul pa de rang gi mtshan nyid kyis yod na ni ngo bo nyid med pa don dam du mi rung la, med na ni 'khrul pa'i phyir dmigs kyang med do, , zhes pa de mi 'thad do,
rows.english: Our answer then would be, Well now, if this mistaken thing is itself something which exists by definition, then it would be wrong to say that the fact that nothing has its own nature is what the "ultimate" refers to. And if on the other hand it didn't exist, then it would be incorrect to say "Because it is mistaken, then what it sees doesn't exist."

rows.acip: DE LTAR NA 'DIR KUN BRTAGS DANG YONGS GRUB GNYIS DON DAM PAR MED CING THA SNYAD DU YOD PA LA SKYON MA BSTAN PAR KUN RDZOB PA'I SHES PA DANG 'KHRUL PA'I SHES PA DON DAM PAR YOD MED LA BRTAGS NAS SKYON BSTAN PA NI, GZHAN DBANG DON DAM PAR MED LA KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA BKAG PA YIN TE, 'DI NYID YONGS GRUB KYI CHOS CAN DANG KUN BRTAGS KYI 'DOGS PA PO DANG GDAGS GZHI YIN PAS MKHAS PA RNAMS GTZO BOR 'DI NYID DON DAM PAR YOD MED LA RTZOD PA YIN NO, ,
rows.wylie: de ltar na 'dir kun brtags dang yongs grub gnyis don dam par med cing tha snyad du yod pa la skyon ma bstan par kun rdzob pa'i shes pa dang 'khrul pa'i shes pa don dam par yod med la brtags nas skyon bstan pa ni, gzhan dbang don dam par med la kun rdzob tu yod pa bkag pa yin te, 'di nyid yongs grub kyi chos can dang kun brtags kyi 'dogs pa po dang gdags gzhi yin pas mkhas pa rnams gtso bor 'di nyid don dam par yod med la rtsod pa yin no,
rows.english: Consider the fact that, in this particular citation, no statement is made criticizing the idea that the pair of constructs and totality are not things which exist ultimately, but do exist nominally. The criticism is rather made through examining the question of whether a deceptive state of mind, and a mistaken state of mind, exist ultimately or not. The point of this approach is to refute the idea that dependent things could be something which did not exist ultimately, but which did exist deceptively. These dependent things are the things that exhibit the quality of totality; they are the ones that apply the constructs; and they too are what the constructs are applied to. And so these are what real thinkers take, primarily, as their subject when they argue about whether things exist ultimately or not.

rows.acip: KHYAD PAR DU GZHAN DBANG THA SNYAD DU YOD PA'I DON 'KHRUL PA'I BLOS DE LA SKYE 'GAG SOGS YOD PAR ZHEN PA TZAM YIN GYI, DNGOS PO LA SKYE 'GAG SOGS MED DO ZHES 'DOD PA NI, GZHAN DBANG LA SKUR 'DEBS KYI MTHAR THUG DE'I RGYU MTSAN GYIS NGO BO NYID GZHAN GNYIS LA YANG SKUR PA BTAB PAS MTSAN NYID GSUM GA LA SKUR 'DEBS CHAD LTA'I GTZO BOR SNGAR BYANG SA LAS BSHAD PA DE YIN ZHING , MDO SDE DGONGS 'GREL NGES DON YIN PAR 'DOD PA'I PHYOGS LA SPANG DU MED PA'I 'GAL BAR SHES PAR GYIS SHIG,
rows.wylie: khyad par du gzhan dbang tha snyad du yod pa'i don 'khrul pa'i blos de la skye 'gag sogs yod par zhen pa tsam yin gyi, dngos po la skye 'gag sogs med do zhes 'dod pa ni, gzhan dbang la skur 'debs kyi mthar thug de'i rgyu mtshan gyis ngo bo nyid gzhan gnyis la yang skur pa btab pas mtshan nyid gsum ga la skur 'debs chad lta'i gtso bor sngar byang sa las bshad pa de yin zhing , mdo sde dgongs 'grel nges don yin par 'dod pa'i phyogs la spang du med pa'i 'gal bar shes par gyis shig
rows.english: Consider especially the position that--when we speak of dependent things as existing nominally--what we mean is that a mistaken state of mind merely imagines that growing and stopping apply to them; and that qualities like growing and stopping don't even exist with functional things. This is the most extreme possible version of discounting dependent things, and for this reason it moreover constitutes discounting the other two natures as well. Being therefore a discounting of all three of the attributes, it is exactly the viewpoint which the Levels of the Bodhisattva mentioned above as being the primary form of the view that all things have stopped. You should finally understand that this is idea would be an inescapable contradiction for anyone who held the position that the Commentary on the True Thought was meant literally. 127 The Asian Classics Institute Course XV: What the Buddha Really Meant Reading Nine: Interpretations of the Independent Group of the Middle-Way School There is no one section of Je Tsongkapa's root text on the Essence of Eloquence that easily presents all the concepts of the Independent group of the Middle-Way School on the subjects covered in the course so far. We therefore begin a group of selections, many from monastic textbooks, which together give us a good overview of the relevant ideas. The first part of the reading helps understand the differences between the Independent group, the Mind-Only School, and the Consequence group on the question of w

rows.acip: ,'O NA MTHONG LAM BAR CHAD MED LAM GYI DUS SU DE'I SPANG BYA MTHONG SPANG MED MOD KYANG , SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL YOD DGOS LA, DE'I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA'I ZAG MED YIN PAS, DE'I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA, DBANG SHES KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA KUN GZHI YANG MI 'DOD PAS DE'I RTEN MED PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM NA, SKYON MED DE DE'I TSE NGA TZAM ZHIG SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL GYI RTEN YIN PA'I PHYIR TE, SPANG GNYEN GZHAN LA YANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O,
rows.wylie: 'o na mthong lam bar chad med lam gyi dus su de'i spang bya mthong spang med mod kyang , sgom spang gi bag la nyal yod dgos la, de'i tshe yid kyi shes pa ni gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i zag med yin pas, de'i ngo bor bag la nyal de gnas pa mi rigs la, dbang shes kyang de'i rten du med cing gzugs kyang de'i rten du mi rigs la kun gzhi yang mi 'dod pas de'i rten med par 'gyur ro snyam na, skyon med de de'i tshe nga tsam zhig sgom spang gi bag la nyal gyi rten yin pa'i phyir te, spang gnyen gzhan la yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o
rows.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things could stay. And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. 24 The Middle-Way School on the Question of Where the Seeds of Karma Stay until They Give their Result

rows.acip: RANG GI NGO BO NYID KYIS GRUB NA GNAS LUGS SU GRUB PAR 'GYUR LA, DE'I TSE 'KHRUL PA LOG PA NA GSAL DU 'GRO DGOS KYI, LDOG PAR MI 'GYUR RO, , ZHES PA'I DON NO,
rows.wylie: rang gi ngo bo nyid kyis grub na gnas lugs su grub par 'gyur la, de'i tshe 'khrul pa log pa na gsal du 'gro dgos kyi, ldog par mi 'gyur ro, , zhes pa'i don no
rows.english: The meaning of the lines is as follows. If things existed in their very essence, then they would exist as some independent reality. If this were so, then when you finally stopped your mistaken states of mind, they would never disappear, although they should have.

rows.acip: DANG PO NI, GAL TE CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MED NA SGYU MA 'DZIN PA'I SHES PA 'KHRUL PA'ANG YOD PA MIN NA SGYU MA BLO GANG GIS DMIGS PAR 'GYUR TE, MI 'GYUR BAS SGYU MA'ANG MED PAR 'GYUR RO ZHE NA 'DI YANG YOD NA RANG BZHIN GYIS YOD DGOS SNYAM PA'I RTZOD PA'O,
rows.wylie: dang po ni, gal te chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis med na sgyu ma 'dzin pa'i shes pa 'khrul pa'ang yod pa min na sgyu ma blo gang gis dmigs par 'gyur te, mi 'gyur bas sgyu ma'ang med par 'gyur ro zhe na 'di yang yod na rang bzhin gyis yod dgos snyam pa'i rtsod pa'o
rows.english: Here is the first of the two. One may begin with the following objection: If there is no object at all that has any nature of its own, then the mistaken state of mind which perceives the illusion cannot exist either. If this were so, then there would be no state of mind that could ever take the illusion as its object. And if this were the case, then the illusion itself could not exist either. This argument too is another version of the idea that, if something exists, it must have a nature of its own.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR KHA CIG GIS MDO 'DI LA BRTEN NAS DUS GSUM PAR GSUNGS PA'I MDO THAMS CAD NGES DON DU BSGRUBS NAS GZHAN SDE'I RIGS CAN BDAG TU SMRA BA LA ZHEN PA RNAMS DRANG BA'I PHYIR DU GSUNGS PA 'GA' ZHIG SGRA JI BZHIN PAR 'DOD CING , CHOS NYID MA GTOGS PA'I CHOS CAN THAMS CAD 'KHRUL PA'I BLOS RLOM PA MA GTOGS PA RANG GI NGO BO GRUB PA CUNG ZAD KYANG MED CING CHOS NYID BDEN PAR GRUB PA'I BDEN MI BDEN RNAM PAR PHYE BA NI SNGAR BSHAD PA'I LEGS PAR RNAM PAR PHYE BA'I DON DU 'DOD DO, ,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir kha cig gis mdo 'di la brten nas dus gsum par gsungs pa'i mdo thams cad nges don du bsgrubs nas gzhan sde'i rigs can bdag tu smra ba la zhen pa rnams drang ba'i phyir du gsungs pa 'ga' zhig sgra ji bzhin par 'dod cing , chos nyid ma gtogs pa'i chos can thams cad 'khrul pa'i blos rlom pa ma gtogs pa rang gi ngo bo grub pa cung zad kyang med cing chos nyid bden par grub pa'i bden mi bden rnam par phye ba ni sngar bshad pa'i legs par rnam par phye ba'i don du 'dod do,
rows.english: Given all this, some have used the wording of this sutra to go on and claim that it proves that everything which Lord Buddha taught during all the periods is meant to be taken literally. These people would then have to say that certain statements which the Buddha made to attract those of other religions who still believed that things could have some self-nature are teachings that we are meant to take on face value. They also say that no object but the real nature of things is anything more than the simple delusion of a mistaken state of mind; these other things have not the slightest bit of an existing nature to them. They say finally that the meaning of "fine distinctions" is the distinction between what exists in truth or not, in the sense of being this one true thing: the real nature of things.

rows.acip: ,'KHRUL PA LAS KYANG CHES 'KHRUL PA, ,SMYO BA LAS KYANG CHES SMYO BA, ,'DI DANG LHAN CIG RTZOD PA 'DI, ,DE LAS KYANG NI SMYO BA 'DRA,
rows.wylie: 'khrul pa las kyang ches 'khrul pa, ,smyo ba las kyang ches smyo ba, ,'di dang lhan cig rtsod pa 'di, ,de las kyang ni smyo ba 'dra
rows.english: You are more mistaken Than mistaken itself; You are more insane Than insanity. And to continue Debating together With someone like you Would be something Even crazier. Actually the debate between totally misunderstanding our world and determining what's really going on should have been a short one: Once we get a rational explanation of how and why things are happening to us, we should rightly change immediately—and that is that. But habit dies hard, and so this debate—which happens within each of us, inside our own thoughts—must continue until the old thought-habits are finally and completely ridiculed and banished.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR RNAM RIG PAS SO SKYE'I RGYUD KYI SNGON 'DZIN DBANG PO'I MNGON SUM YANG RANG GI SNANG YUL LA 'KHRUL BAR 'DOD CING, DES DRANGS NAS SKYES PA'I RTOG PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I CHOS KYI BDAG 'DZIN DU 'DOD DO,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir rnam rig pas so skye'i rgyud kyi sngon 'dzin dbang po'i mngon sum yang rang gi snang yul la 'khrul bar 'dod cing, des drangs nas skyes pa'i rtog pa de zhen yul la 'khrul pa'i chos kyi bdag 'dzin du 'dod do
rows.english: And so it is that the Mentalists believe that even direct sense perception in the mind of a normal person is mistaken towards its object, as this object appears to the perception. And then the thought that arises inspired by this perception—the one which is mistaken about what it thinks it sees—is, they say, what we're referring to when we talk about the “tendency to believe in some self-nature to things.”

rows.acip: NUS TE, BSHAD MA THAG PA LTAR GZUGS SOGS RANG 'DZIN RTOG PA'I ZHEN GZHIR RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PAR KHEGS PA NA, DE'I TSE SNANG BA LTAR ZHEN PA'I RTOG PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PAR 'GRUB LA,
rows.wylie: nus te, bshad ma thag pa ltar gzugs sogs rang 'dzin rtog pa'i zhen gzhir rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub par khegs pa na, de'i tshe snang ba ltar zhen pa'i rtog pa de zhen yul la 'khrul par 'grub la
rows.english: Here's how it's done. As I've just explained, we can disprove the way in which we tend to think that things like form exist, by definition, as the objects of our perceptions. And we thus further prove that these thoughts are mistaken towards what they are considering; believing that they exist as they appear to.

rows.acip: DE GRUB PA'I STOBS KYIS DE LTAR SNANG BA'I DBANG SHES RNAMS KYANG RANG GI SNANG YUL LA 'KHRUL PAR 'GRUB,
rows.wylie: de grub pa'i stobs kyis de ltar snang ba'i dbang shes rnams kyang rang gi snang yul la 'khrul par 'grub
rows.english: Proving that they are mistaken proves, in turn, that the sense consciousnesses are also mistaken, when things appear that way to them.

rows.acip: [N54] ,SEMS KYI GNYIS MED DAG PA YIS, ,SEMS NI 'KHRUL PAR 'GYUR MA YIN, ,'KHRUL PA'I RANG BZHIN NYID STONG BAS, ,DES NA SEMS NI MTHONG MA YIN,
rows.wylie: [n54] ,sems kyi gnyis med dag pa yis, ,sems ni 'khrul par 'gyur ma yin, ,'khrul pa'i rang bzhin nyid stong bas, ,des na sems ni mthong ma yin
rows.english: When the mind Comes at last to purity, Where no more two are there, Then it reaches a state Where now it is empty Of that one mistaken nature— And thus no mind is seen.

rows.acip: [C3] 'ON KYANG, DE'I TSE NYON YID RDZAS RGYUN CHAD PA'I TSUL GYIS SPANGS PA MA YIN TE, DE'I TSE NA YID GSAL RIG TZAM GYI NGO BOR GNAS GYUR NAS SLAR YANG YID KYI RNAM SHES 'KHRUL PA SKYE BA'I BDAG RKYEN BYED PA'I PHYIR,
rows.wylie: [c3] 'on kyang, de'i tshe nyon yid rdzas rgyun chad pa'i tshul gyis spangs pa ma yin te, de'i tshe na yid gsal rig tsam gyi ngo bor gnas gyur nas slar yang yid kyi rnam shes 'khrul pa skye ba'i bdag rkyen byed pa'i phyir
rows.english: We cannot say though at this point that we have rid ourselves of these negative emotions in the sense that we have cut off their substantial flow.  If that were the case, then this state of mind would transform into nothing more than raw clear knowing; which would then allow it to serve as a condition, contained within our being, for mistaken states of consciousness to arise once again.

rows.acip: [D21] NOR BU CHU SHEL DANG DNGUL LA SOGS PA PHAN TSUN SGRO MI 'DOGS BAR JI LTA BAR SHES BA {%PA} BZHIN DU BDEN SNANG GI 'KHRUL PA'I MTSAN MA MTHA' DAG SPANGS PA SGYU MA LTA BU'I BDAG NYID DU GYUR PA'I CHOS THAMS CAD BDEN MED DU SNANG BA'I BLO RNAM PAR MI RTOG PA
rows.wylie: [d21] nor bu chu shel dang dngul la sogs pa phan tshun sgro mi 'dogs bar ji lta bar shes ba {%pa} bzhin du bden snang gi 'khrul pa'i mtshan ma mtha' dag spangs pa sgyu ma lta bu'i bdag nyid du gyur pa'i chos thams cad bden med du snang ba'i blo rnam par mi rtog pa
rows.english: What happens with them is comparable to what happens with a person who learns not to exaggerate the reality of crystal and silver—or other such substances—either way: thinking the crystal is silver, or that the silver is crystal.  They achieve a state of mind which is no longer immersed in mistaken thoughts: they eliminate every trace of the error of seeing things appear as real; and their thoughts embrace the idea that no object in the universe has any reality—they are all entities which are just the same as a magical illusion.

rows.acip: BDEN 'DZIN NYON MONGS SU 'JOG PA'I LUGS 'DI LA, NYON MONGS ZAG MED KYI LAM GYIS SPONG BA NA, BDEN 'DZIN RE'I SA BON SPONG DGOS PAS SA BON DE LAS GZHAN PA'I GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS SHES SGRIB TU BZHAG PA'I PHYOGS RE YANG GTAN ZAD MI NUS PAS, NYON MONGS THAMS CAD MA ZAD BAR DU SHES SGRIB MI SPONG BA'I PHYIR, SHES SGRIB NI DAG PA SA GSUM GYI SKABS SU SPONG NGO,,
rows.wylie: bden 'dzin nyon mongs su 'jog pa'i lugs 'di la, nyon mongs zag med kyi lam gyis spong ba na, bden 'dzin re'i sa bon spong dgos pas sa bon de las gzhan pa'i gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags shes sgrib tu bzhag pa'i phyogs re yang gtan zad mi nus pas, nyon mongs thams cad ma zad bar du shes sgrib mi spong ba'i phyir, shes sgrib ni dag pa sa gsum gyi skabs su spong ngo
rows.english: Here in this system, where holding that things are real is classified as a negative emotion, each seed of holding things this way must be eliminated where negativities are eliminated by the path of the immaculate. But not all the different propensities for seeing things in a mistaken way—with a discrepancy—which are other than these seeds, and which we classify as obstacles to omniscience, can at that point be eliminated permanently. As such, we cannot rid ourselves of the obstacles to omniscience until we finish off all the negative emotions; and therefore it is during the three pure levels that we rid ourselves of these omniscience obstacles.

rows.acip: DE YANG THOG MA MED PA'I 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS YONGS SU SMIN PA'I DBANG GIS BYUNG LA, DES KYANG SROG CHAGS THAMS CAD LA YANG DAG PAR DNGOS PO'I BDAG NYID LTA BUR NYE BAR BSTAN PA MTHONG BAR 'GYUR TE, DE'I PHYIR DE DAG GI BSAM PA'I DBANG GIS DNGOS PO BRDZUN PA'I NGO BO THAMS CAD NI, KUN RDZOB TU YOD PA KHO NA'O ZHES BYA'O, ZHES GSUNGS SO,,
rows.wylie: de yang thog ma med pa'i 'khrul pa'i bag chags yongs su smin pa'i dbang gis byung la, des kyang srog chags thams cad la yang dag par dngos po'i bdag nyid lta bur nye bar bstan pa mthong bar 'gyur te, de'i phyir de dag gi bsam pa'i dbang gis dngos po brdzun pa'i ngo bo thams cad ni, kun rdzob tu yod pa kho na'o zhes bya'o, zhes gsungs so
rows.english: All of this is coming from the ripening of seeds in our mind which, from time with no beginning, have forced us to see things in a mistaken way. And because of these seeds, what is presented to the minds of every single living creature is a reality that looks as though it is composed of things that exist in & of themselves—and then we see it that way. All these things whose very nature is to lie to us—which are nothing more than creations of our mind—are, the sutra is saying, nothing but things that exist in a deceptive way.

rows.acip: SPRUL GZHI RTA GLANG DU SNANG BA NA, DPER NA THAG PA LA SPRUL {%SBRUL} DU 'KHRUL PA'I TSE SHES PA DE'I NGOR THAG PA SBRUL YIN GYI, SPYIR SBRUL MIN ZHES ZER BA BZHIN DU,
rows.wylie: sprul gzhi rta glang du snang ba na, dper na thag pa la sprul {%sbrul} du 'khrul pa'i tshe shes pa de'i ngor thag pa sbrul yin gyi, spyir sbrul min zhes zer ba bzhin du
rows.english: Let's consider what's happening when the object the magician is using appears as though it were a horse, or elephant. We can think of a parallel case, where a person has mistaken a piece of rope for a snake. We can say that—to their perceptions—the rope is a snake; but that, generally speaking, the rope is not a snake.

rows.acip: DES NA SPRUL GZHI RTA GLANG DU SNANG BAR 'JOG NUS PA DE, ,SGYU MA MKHAN LTAR NA BLO 'KHRUL PA LA DE LTAR SNANG BA'I DBANG GIS 'JOG GI ,DE LTAR MIN PAR SPRUL GZHI RANG GI SDOD LUGS KYI DBANG GIS 'JOG PA MIN NO,,
rows.wylie: des na sprul gzhi rta glang du snang bar 'jog nus pa de, ,sgyu ma mkhan ltar na blo 'khrul pa la de ltar snang ba'i dbang gis 'jog gi ,de ltar min par sprul gzhi rang gi sdod lugs kyi dbang gis 'jog pa min no
rows.english: Thus can we establish that the token is appearing as the elephant; and from the magician's point of view, the appearance of the object in this way is established with regard to a mistaken state of mind. Suppose it were not this way: then the appearance of the token as an elephant would have to be established through some kind of natural existence of its own—but that's not how it is.

rows.acip: ,NYID KYI SGRAS NI SHES PA DE RNAMS 'KHRUL PAR 'JOG PA LA NI, THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MA NYID KYIS CHOG GI RIGS SHES LA MI LTOS PAR STON PA'O,,
rows.wylie: nyid kyi sgras ni shes pa de rnams 'khrul par 'jog pa la ni, tha snyad pa'i tshad ma nyid kyis chog gi rigs shes la mi ltos par ston pa'o
rows.english: The expression “even just” here is meant to indicate that it's enough here—when we establish these states of mind as mistaken—to utilize even just a nominal form of accurate perception; it's not that, rather, we would have to rely upon some exploration of the way things are.

rows.acip: KUN RDZOB NI THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS 'JOG DGOS PA'I PHYIR LOG PA'I KUN RDZOB 'JOG NA YANG DE LA BLTOS NAS 'JOG DGOS NA, MA RIG PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PA NI 'KHRUL PAR THA SNYAD PA'I TSAD MAS MI 'GRUB PA'I PHYIR RO,,
rows.wylie: kun rdzob ni tha snyad pa'i tshad mas 'jog dgos pa'i phyir log pa'i kun rdzob 'jog na yang de la bltos nas 'jog dgos na, ma rig pa'i bag chags kyis bslad pa ni 'khrul par tha snyad pa'i tshad mas mi 'grub pa'i phyir ro
rows.english: Deceptive reality is something which must be established by a nominal form of accurate perception; as such, if we were to establish a mistaken form of deceptive reality, that too would have to be established relative to this type of perception. It is not the case then that we could ever use a nominal form of accurate perception to determine that something infected by deep seeds of misunderstanding was mistaken. Views inspired by sleep

rows.acip: 'DIS NI LUGS 'DIS BLO 'KHRUL PA CIG GI NGOR YOD PA LA, KUN RDZOB TU YOD PAR 'JOG ZER BA LEGS PAR BKAG GO
rows.wylie: 'dis ni lugs 'dis blo 'khrul pa cig gi ngor yod pa la, kun rdzob tu yod par 'jog zer ba legs par bkag go
rows.english: This in itself is enough to disprove, perfectly, the claim by this system that a thing is established as existing deceptively relative to the perceptions of a mistaken state of mind.

rows.acip: GANG ZAG DANG CHOS RANG BZHIN GYIS GRUB PA NI, DE 'GOG PA'I RIGS PA RNAMS KYIS KHEGS PAR 'GYUR ZHING, DE'I TSE DE LTAR 'DZIN PA DE ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I BDEN 'DZIN DU 'GRUB LA, DE GRUB NA GANG ZAG DANG CHOS GNYIS BDEN GRUB TU 'DZIN PA BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS SU 'GRUB BO,,
rows.wylie: gang zag dang chos rang bzhin gyis grub pa ni, de 'gog pa'i rigs pa rnams kyis khegs par 'gyur zhing, de'i tshe de ltar 'dzin pa de zhen yul la 'khrul pa'i bden 'dzin du 'grub la, de grub na gang zag dang chos gnyis bden grub tu 'dzin pa bdag 'dzin gnyis su 'grub bo
rows.english: They refute the idea that the person & things could exist through some nature of their own by employing different forms of reasoning which disproves it. They would establish, at this point, the tendency to hold these things this way as being a tendency to hold that things are real where we are mistaken about the object that we think we see. Once this is established, they establish that the tendencies to hold the person and things as being real are what constitute the two forms of holding that things are themselves.

rows.acip: NYON MONGS KYI SA BON LA BAG CHAGS SU BZHAG PA CIG DANG, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON MIN PA'I BAG CHAGS GNYIS LAS SHES SGRIB TU 'JOG PA NI PHYI MA STE, NYON MONGS KYI SA BON THAMS CAD ZAD PAS BDEN 'DZIN MI SKYE YANG, BAG CHAGS KYIS BSLAD PAS SNANG YUL LA 'KHRUL PA'I BLO SKYED PA'O,,
rows.wylie: nyon mongs kyi sa bon la bag chags su bzhag pa cig dang, nyon mongs kyi sa bon min pa'i bag chags gnyis las shes sgrib tu 'jog pa ni phyi ma ste, nyon mongs kyi sa bon thams cad zad pas bden 'dzin mi skye yang, bag chags kyis bslad pas snang yul la 'khrul pa'i blo skyed pa'o
rows.english: Deep seeds can be divided into two types: those which can be classified as seeds for negative emotions, and those which are not seeds for negative emotions. Those that we classify as obstacles to knowledge are the latter. That is, when we have finished off all our seeds for negative emotions, the tendency to hold things as real no longer arises; but because we are still infected by deep seeds, we do experience the arisal of states of mind that are mistaken towards the object as it appears to them.

rows.acip: DE LTAR NA DBANG SHES 'KHRUL PA LA SNANG BA'I BYAD DANG ZLA GNYIS DANG SKRA SHAD SOGS NI, DBANG PO LA 'PHRAL GYI GNOD PA MED PA'I SHES PA LNGA LA SNANG BA'I RANG GI MTSAN NYID KYIS GRUB PA DANG 'DRA'O,,
rows.wylie: de ltar na dbang shes 'khrul pa la snang ba'i byad dang zla gnyis dang skra shad sogs ni, dbang po la 'phral gyi gnod pa med pa'i shes pa lnga la snang ba'i rang gi mtshan nyid kyis grub pa dang 'dra'o
rows.english: And so what's being said here is that when our sense perceptions are mistaken, and an object which is actually just a reflection in the mirror appears to us—or we see things like the two moons, or a hair lying there—it is similar to the case with our five sense perceptions when they are not affected by any adventitious defect, but things appear to them to exist by definition.

rows.acip: THAG PA'I RGYU MTSAN CAN GYI SBRUL DU 'KHRUL BA NI THAG PA MED PA'I GZHIR MI SKYE LA, BUM PA LA SOGS PA'I RGYU MTSAN CAN GYI 'KHRUL PA NI, SA LA SOGS PA MED PA'I NAM MKHA'I PHYOGS SU SKYE BAR MI 'GYUR BA BZHIN DU, PHYI ROL GYI DON MED NA SNGON PO LA SOGS PA PHYI ROL TU 'KHRUL BA'I RTOG PA 'KHRUL GZHI JI 'DRA BA ZHIG GI RGYU CAN DU 'GYUR,
rows.wylie: thag pa'i rgyu mtshan can gyi sbrul du 'khrul ba ni thag pa med pa'i gzhir mi skye la, bum pa la sogs pa'i rgyu mtshan can gyi 'khrul pa ni, sa la sogs pa med pa'i nam mkha'i phyogs su skye bar mi 'gyur ba bzhin du, phyi rol gyi don med na sngon po la sogs pa phyi rol tu 'khrul ba'i rtog pa 'khrul gzhi ji 'dra ba zhig gi rgyu can du 'gyur
rows.english: Mistaking a rope as a snake due to the proximity of the rope is not something that ever occurs in a location where there is no rope. And a perceptual error founded in a water pitcher or the like is not something that would ever arise in the middle of the sky, where there are no elements of earth or the like. The case here is just the same; that is, if there are no outer objects, then what would be the cause behind a perception which mistakenly took blue or the like as existing on the outside? How could the circumstances that allowed the error be present?

rows.acip: CI STE RMI LAM NA RNAM PAR SHES PA 'KHRUL PA MED NA, DE'I SAD PAS RMI LAM GYI DUS GYI NYAMS SU MYONG BA PHYIS DRAN PAR MI 'GYUR RO SNYAM NA,
rows.wylie: ci ste rmi lam na rnam par shes pa 'khrul pa med na, de'i sad pas rmi lam gyi dus gyi nyams su myong ba phyis dran par mi 'gyur ro snyam na
rows.english: At this point, the following thought might then occur to one: If there exists no mistaken awareness within a dream, then when we wake from the dream we shouldn't be able to remember—later on—what we experienced during the dream.

rows.acip: DE'I PHYIR BDAG 'DZIN GNYIS LTA BU LA YANG BDAG GNYIS KYI SNANG BA MNGON SUM DU 'CHAR LA, DE'I TSE GZHAL BYA SNANG BA MNGON GYUR DE YUL CAN DES 'GRUB PA SOGS SNGAR DANG 'DRA STE, DES ZHEN YUL LA 'KHRUL PA GZHAN YANG SHES PAR BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: de'i phyir bdag 'dzin gnyis lta bu la yang bdag gnyis kyi snang ba mngon sum du 'char la, de'i tshe gzhal bya snang ba mngon gyur de yul can des 'grub pa sogs sngar dang 'dra ste, des zhen yul la 'khrul pa gzhan yang shes par bya'o
rows.english: As such, we can say even with things like the two forms of the tendency to grasp to some self-nature of things that the appearance of two “selfs” here is made directly. And we can also say at that point things like the fact that the object under consideration is making its appearance directly is confirmed by the subject state of mind; just as we did this earlier. And from this we can also understand moreover that this state of mind is mistaken towards the object that it thinks it sees.

rows.acip: KHO BO CAG NI KUN RDZOB 'KHRUL PA'I SNANG BA RANG RGYUD LA BZLOG PA'I PHYIR SHIN TU TSEGS CHE BAS LAM SGOM PA LA GNAS PAR 'GYUR GYI, GAL TE KHYOD LA 'JIG RTEN GYIS MI GNOD NA, KHYOD KYIS 'JIG RTEN NYID LA LTOS NAS KUN RDZOB 'DI NI DGAG PAR GYIS SHIG ,DE KHYOD KYI RIGS PAS 'GOG NUS NA NGAS KYANG KHYOD LA STONGS GDAB PA STE GROGS BYA'O,,
rows.wylie: kho bo cag ni kun rdzob 'khrul pa'i snang ba rang rgyud la bzlog pa'i phyir shin tu tshegs che bas lam sgom pa la gnas par 'gyur gyi, gal te khyod la 'jig rten gyis mi gnod na, khyod kyis 'jig rten nyid la ltos nas kun rdzob 'di ni dgag par gyis shig ,de khyod kyi rigs pas 'gog nus na ngas kyang khyod la stongs gdab pa ste grogs bya'o
rows.english: We for our part have kept up our practice of the path with incredibly great effort, in order to put a stop to the mistaken appearance of deceptive reality within our own minds. If what the world says is not something that could call your ideas into question, then you can go ahead and deny this deceptive reality relative to the world itself. If you find that this is something that you can deny with your particular reasoning, then I will gladly “join hands with you”—meaning, I will accompany you.

rows.acip: GZHAN GYI LUGS KYIS NI PHYI ROL CHA MED KHEGS NA SNANG BA LA MA 'KHRUL BA'I DBANG SHES KHEGS, DBANG SHES 'KHRUL PAS DON 'JOG MI NUS PAS PHYI DON KHEGS SO SNYAM DU BSAMS SO,,
rows.wylie: gzhan gyi lugs kyis ni phyi rol cha med khegs na snang ba la ma 'khrul ba'i dbang shes khegs, dbang shes 'khrul pas don 'jog mi nus pas phyi don khegs so snyam du bsams so
rows.english: According to the other side here, you deny an awareness of the senses which is unmistaken towards what appears to it, when you deny that outside objects have no sides to them. A sense awareness which is mistaken is not capable of establishing its object; and so one would think that outer objects had been denied.

rows.acip: 'DIR NI DBANG SHES 'KHRUL PAS GZHAL BYA BDEN PA 'JOG MI NUS KYANG, GZHAL BYA BRDZUN PA 'JOG PA LA DE GROGS SU SONG NGO SNYAM DU DGONGS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'dir ni dbang shes 'khrul pas gzhal bya bden pa 'jog mi nus kyang, gzhal bya brdzun pa 'jog pa la de grogs su song ngo snyam du dgongs so
rows.english: Here we can say that a sense awareness which is mistaken cannot establish reality as the object under its consideration. And the thinking here is that—when we seek to establish an object of consideration which is deceptive—it would have to serve in an assisting role.

rows.acip: 'O NA MTHONG LAM BAR CHAD MED LAM GYI DUS SU DE'I SPANG BYA MTHONG SPANG MED MOD KYANG, SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL YOD DGOS LA DE'I TSE YID KYI SHES PA NI GNYIS SNANG 'KHRUL PA'I BAG CHAGS KYIS MA BSLAD PA'I ZAG MED YIN PAS DE'I NGO BOR BAG LA NYAL DE GNAS PA MI RIGS LA DBANG SHES KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MED CING GZUGS KYANG DE'I RTEN DU MI RIGS LA KUN GZHI YANG MI 'DOD PAS DE'I RTEN MED PAR 'GYUR RO SNYAM NA SKYON MED DE DE'I TSE NGA TZAM ZHIG SGOM SPANG GI BAG LA NYAL GYI RTEN YIN PA'I PHYIR TE SPANG GNYEN GZHAN LA YANG DE BZHIN DU SHES PAR BYA'O
rows.wylie: 'o na mthong lam bar chad med lam gyi dus su de'i spang bya mthong spang med mod kyang, sgom spang gi bag la nyal yod dgos la de'i tshe yid kyi shes pa ni gnyis snang 'khrul pa'i bag chags kyis ma bslad pa'i zag med yin pas de'i ngo bor bag la nyal de gnas pa mi rigs la dbang shes kyang de'i rten du med cing gzugs kyang de'i rten du mi rigs la kun gzhi yang mi 'dod pas de'i rten med par 'gyur ro snyam na skyon med de de'i tshe nga tsam zhig sgom spang gi bag la nyal gyi rten yin pa'i phyir te spang gnyen gzhan la yang de bzhin du shes par bya'o
rows.english: One might wonder about something else: Let's talk about the period while you are in the "uninterrupted" stage of the path of seeing [the actual direct perception of emptiness]. I can accept that at this point the negative thoughts eliminated by this path are no longer present, but we would have to say that the negative things eliminated by the path of habituation are still there, in a dormant way. At this particular point in time, the consciousness of the mind is unstained, unaffected by the mental seed which causes the mistaken state of mind where the appearance and actuality of things are different from one another. As such none of these things could lie dormant here, due to its very quality at the time. There is no consciousness of the senses that could act as the basis for those mental seeds, and it would be improper to say that physical form could ever provide such a basis either. According to you, moreover, there's no foundation consciousness. I would have to think then that there is no basis at all where these dormant things And yet there is no such problem, for at this point in time it is the simple "me" which is providing the basis for the dormant things eliminated by the path of habituation to stay. You can apply this reasoning as well to all the other cases involving things to be eliminated, and the antidotes which eliminate them. Selection Three: The Middle-Way School on the question of where the seeds of karma stay until they give their result

rows.acip: SPANG BYA SPONG TSUL SLOB DPON LEGS LDAN 'BYED SOGS KYIS 'KHRUL PAS 'KHRUL PA SPONG BAR DPE'I SGO NAS BZHAG PA NI SO SO SKYE BO'I SKABS SU DANG,

rows.english: Moreover, Master Bhavaviveka describes a way in which undesirable qualities are eliminated by people who are still at the point where they have not yet seen emptiness directly. He uses an example in which a mistaken state of mind is used to eliminate a mistake.

rows.acip: DE NI 'DU BYED LA SOGS PA NI MA RIG PAS BRTAGS PA YIN PAS BLO 'KHRUL PA LA SNANG GI ,'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG GIS GZIGS PA LA MA YIN TE,

rows.english: What this means is that fresh karma and the rest of those links-as things which are only imputed to exist by misunderstanding-are something that makes its appearance to a mistaken state of mind. It is not something that presents itself to the sight of a realized being who is in that deep meditation upon emptiness.

rows.acip: DE 'KHRUL NGO KHO NAR KHAS LEN GYI, RANG LUGS LA YOD PA MA YIN TE, BLO MA 'KHRUL PA 'PHAGS PA'I MNYAM GZHAG YIN PAS DES MA GZIGS PAS SO ZHE NA,

rows.english: They might reply with: But they accept dependence as something that can make its appearance only to a mistaken state of mind; in their own system then, dependence is something that has no existence. And that's because it cannot be observed by a truly unmistaken state of mind: the deep meditation of a realized being.

rows.english: (10) There do exist accurate perceptions which are mistaken about the object they are considering.

Once one has reached the union of the two where there is still further learning to be done, you practice the clear light. This allows you to clean yourself of the mental seeds for inconsistent, mistaken perception.

rows.english: Just how is it that we are tormented so unbearably by this pain?  This cycle of pain that we live in is like a prison: a place where those who have done wrong are detained.  And all of us here--due to negative seeds in our mind that make us see things wrongly--entertain a completely mistaken vision of this place, where we see it as though it were a garden of earthly delights.  What we need then is to relinquish this vision and find, or discover, the treasure of the jewels of the realized: high qualities including all three of the higher trainings (the higher training of leading an ethical life, and so on)--as well as faith, morality, learning, generosity, wisdom, consideration, and shame.

parameters: The mind is the main thing; and to show this, the following explanation appears in the scripture: The world, in the form of those who live in it, finds its very being through the power of the karma they have collected with their minds, and through the bad thoughts in their minds. All the vast multitude of worlds too, in the form of the places where these beings live, have been put there, have been produced, by the collective karma of these same beings, and no one else--by the karma within their own minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

rows.english: As for the disc of water and gold, a pillar of rain so dense it looks like the shaft of a oxcart falls then upon that massive disc of wind. This causes the formation of a great disc of water possessing an inner base of gold. The measure of this water in its thickness is equal to one million, twenty thousand yojana [about 4.6 million miles].

All the vast multitude of worlds too, in the form of the places where these beings live, have been put there, have been produced, by the collective karma of these same beings, and no one else--by the karma within their own minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."

rows.acip: ,LONGS SPYOD RDZOGS PA'I SKU NI GNAS NGES PA 'OG MIN KHO NAR BZHUGS PA SOGS NGES PA LNGA LDAN YIN LA,
rows.wylie: longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku ni gnas nges pa 'og min kho nar bzhugs pa sogs nges pa lnga ldan yin la
rows.english: The holy body which is complete in all enjoyments is defined as being fixed, in five different ways.  It is (1) fixed in its location, because it stays only in the enlightened Paradise Below No Other.  The physical body here is also fixed, because (2) it invariably possesses all the signs and marks of an Enlightened Being—and these indications are both distinct and complete, in the sense of never being partial.  The retinue that accompanies this body is (3) invariably composed of bodhisattvas who are also realized beings.  This body is, further, (4) fixed in the sense of what teachings it presents to disciples; invariably, those of the greater way.  And then finally, (5) the duration here is fixed: the body will remain and serve, so long as there is even a single living being who has not yet achieved total enlightenment.

rows.acip: [A15] NGES PA LNGA YANG YOD DE, GNAS NGES PA 'OG MIN LHUG {%STUG} PO BKOD PA KHO NAR BZHUGS PA, 'KHOR NGES PA BYANG 'PHAGS SHA STAG GIS BSKOR PA, CHOS NGES PA THEG CHEN GYI CHOS 'BA' ZHIG GSUNGS PA, SKU NGES PA MTSAN DPE GSAL RDZOGS KYIS SPRAS PA, DUS NGES PA 'KHOR BA MA STONG GI BAR DU BZHUGS PA RNAMS SU YOD PA'I PHYIR TE,
rows.wylie: [a15] nges pa lnga yang yod de, gnas nges pa 'og min lhug {%stug} po bkod pa kho nar bzhugs pa, 'khor nges pa byang 'phags sha stag gis bskor pa, chos nges pa theg chen gyi chos 'ba' zhig gsungs pa, sku nges pa mtshan dpe gsal rdzogs kyis spras pa, dus nges pa 'khor ba ma stong gi bar du bzhugs pa rnams su yod pa'i phyir te
rows.english: Here are the five fixed qualities of the paradise body: 1) Its location is fixed, in that the body resides only in that divine realm called “The Mass of Clouds, below No Other.” 2) The beings in attendance to it are fixed, for they are invariably realized beings who are bodhisattvas. 3) The teachings it gives are fixed, for this body speaks only teachings of the greater way. 4) The appearance of this body is fixed, because it is always adorned with clear and complete versions of the physical signs and marks of an Enlightened Being. 5) The duration of this body is fixed, for it will last until the cycle of pain is emptied of living beings.

rows.acip: 'OG MIN KHO NAR ZHES GSUNGS PAS NI SNGAR SANGS MA RGYAS PA GSAR DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I RTEN LA 'OG MIN PA DGOS PAR STON LA, SNGON SANGS RGYAS ZIN GSAR DU 'TSANG RGYA BA'I TSUL STON PA 'DOD PA KHAMS SU MDZAD PA YIN TE, PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I THEG PA'I LUGS SO,,
rows.wylie: 'og min kho nar zhes gsungs pas ni sngar sangs ma rgyas pa gsar du 'tshang rgya ba'i rten la 'og min pa dgos par ston la, sngon sangs rgyas zin gsar du 'tshang rgya ba'i tshul ston pa 'dod pa khams su mdzad pa yin te, pha rol tu phyin pa'i theg pa'i lugs so
rows.english: When we use the expression “only in the One Below No Other,” what we are indicating is that a person who has never achieved Buddhahood before must first attain this state in a body & mind located in the level of Below No Other. If though a person has already achieved enlightenment, and is going to pretend to reach it anew, then they do so in the desire realm. That is, at least, according to the way of the perfections.

rows.acip: PHEEm, RANG GI THUGS KA'I BAm YIG LAS 'OD ZER 'PHROS PAS, 'OG MIN NAS RJE BTZUN RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA LA, BLA MA YI DAM SANGS RGYAS BYANG SEMS DPA' BO MKHA' 'GRO CHOS DANG 'JIG RTEN SKYONG BA'I TSOGS KYIS BSKOR BA MDUN GYI NAM MKHAR SPYAN DRANGS,
rows.wylie: pheeM, rang gi thugs ka'i baM yig las 'od zer 'phros pas, 'og min nas rje btsun rdo rje rnal 'byor ma la, bla ma yi dam sangs rgyas byang sems dpa' bo mkha' 'gro chos dang 'jig rten skyong ba'i tshogs kyis bskor ba mdun gyi nam mkhar spyan drangs
rows.english: Phem! Light shines forth From the letter vam Within my heart; It flies to the Heaven Below No Other, And brings back the Holy Angel of Diamond, Surrounded by the Lamas, Close Angels, Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Warriors and their Angels, And the assembled Protectors Of both the Teachings And the world.

rows.acip: ,H'Um 'OG MIN BDE CHEN DAG PA'I PHO BRANG NAS, ,RNAM SNANG THUGS LAS SPRUL PA'I MTHU BO CHE, ,BSTAN SRUNG KUN GYI GTZO BO RDO RJE GUR, ,DPAL LDAN MGON PO 'DIR BYON MCHOD GTOR BZHES,
rows.wylie: hUM 'og min bde chen dag pa'i pho brang nas, ,rnam snang thugs las sprul pa'i mthu bo che, ,bstan srung kun gyi gtso bo rdo rje gur, ,dpal ldan mgon po 'dir byon mchod gtor bzhes
rows.english: Hung, Come, Canopy of Diamond, Head of all Protectors of the Teachings, Great Leader, Sent out from the heart Of the Buddha, Appearances, Who sits in the palace Of the Heaven Below No Other, Great bliss, and pure; Glorious Savior, Come, partake, Of the torma offerings.

rows.acip: GZHAN LHA MI DANG DRANG SRONG SER SKYA SOGS KYIS KYANG DE LTAR MI NUS, DE YANG BDAG CAG GI STON PA MNYAM MED SH'A KYA'I RGYAL PO DE NYID KYIS 'GRO BA RNAMS KYI DON DU DANG PO THUGS BSKYED, BAR DU TSOGS BSAGS, MTHAR 'OG MIN DU MNGON PAR RDZOGS PAR SANGS RGYAS NAS 'DZAM GLING 'DIR MDZAD PA BCU GNYIS KYI RNAM PAR ROL TE GDUL BYA RNAMS THAR PA DANG THAMS CAD MKHYEN PA THOB PHYIR CHOS 'KHOR BSKOR NAS CHOS GSUNGS PA NI THAR 'DOD RNAMS KYI 'JUG DOGS NYAG GCIG YIN TE,
rows.wylie: gzhan lha mi dang drang srong ser skya sogs kyis kyang de ltar mi nus, de yang bdag cag gi ston pa mnyam med shA kya'i rgyal po de nyid kyis 'gro ba rnams kyi don du dang po thugs bskyed, bar du tshogs bsags, mthar 'og min du mngon par rdzogs par sangs rgyas nas 'dzam gling 'dir mdzad pa bcu gnyis kyi rnam par rol te gdul bya rnams thar pa dang thams cad mkhyen pa thob phyir chos 'khor bskor nas chos gsungs pa ni thar 'dod rnams kyi 'jug dogs nyag gcig yin te
rows.english: Nobody else--man or god, monk or layman, accomplished saint or whatever--can do it.  For it was only our matchless Teacher, the King of the Shakyas, who for the sake of all living beings first made the Wish; who in the interim collected masses of virtue; who at the end reached total enlightenment in the Heaven Below No Other. He then came here to Earth, to Dzambu, and put on His play of the twelve mighty deeds of the Buddha; and it was here that He turned the Wheel of the Dharma, so that His disciples could reach liberation and omniscience.  The Dharma that He spoke is the one and only entrance for those who hope to achieve liberation.

rows.acip: DE LA BRTEN NAS 'OG MIN GYI RNAL 'BYOR MA SOGS KYANG GLING GZHAN LA MI 'BYON PAR 'DZAM BU GLING GI RNAL 'BYOR PHO MO BYIN GYIS RLOB CING GROGS MDZAD CING, DE'I PHYIR LAM SNA MA ZIN PAS TSE GCIG LA SANGS RGYAS THOB NA 'DZAM BU GLING GI MI MNGAL SKYES KHAMS DRUG LDAN PA YIN PAS KHYAB CING, DMIGS BSAL SNGON GYI BAG CHAGS SAD PA RE GNYIS GZUGS KHAMS SOGS LA'ANG 'BYUNG NGO,
rows.wylie: de la brten nas 'og min gyi rnal 'byor ma sogs kyang gling gzhan la mi 'byon par 'dzam bu gling gi rnal 'byor pho mo byin gyis rlob cing grogs mdzad cing, de'i phyir lam sna ma zin pas tshe gcig la sangs rgyas thob na 'dzam bu gling gi mi mngal skyes khams drug ldan pa yin pas khyab cing, dmigs bsal sngon gyi bag chags sad pa re gnyis gzugs khams sogs la'ang 'byung ngo
rows.english: Due to all this, Angels of Diamond from the Paradise Below No Other don't bother going to other continents.  Rather they come to yogis and yoginis who live in this world of the Jambudvipa, to bless us and befriend us.   We can say then that--if a person who is not already very far along in the path manages to achieve enlightenment within a single lifetime--then they are necessarily someone who is a human, born from the womb, and possessed of the six elements.  There are only very occasional exceptions to this rule: a person or two in the form realm who has seeds from past lives that suddenly ripen, and then they reach Buddhahood.

rows.acip: DES PHRA BA BAR DO'I LUS MTSON PA STE GZHI DUS SU BAR SRID SBYONG BAS NA BAR DO LONGS SKU'I LAM 'KHYER ZHES BYA, LAM DUS SU DAG MA DAG GI SGYU LUS DANG, 'BRAS DUS SU 'OG MIN DU LONGS SKU 'GRUB PA'I RGYUR 'GYUR RO,
rows.wylie: des phra ba bar do'i lus mtshon pa ste gzhi dus su bar srid sbyong bas na bar do longs sku'i lam 'khyer zhes bya, lam dus su dag ma dag gi sgyu lus dang, 'bras dus su 'og min du longs sku 'grub pa'i rgyur 'gyur ro
rows.english: The fact that the vam syllable is so tiny represents the subtle body of an intermediate being.  And so with reference to the original state you are trying to transform your life in the intermediate state, and this is why we call this practice "using the intermediate state as a path to the Enjoyment Body."  This practice acts as a cause for attaining your impure rainbow body and your totally pure rainbow body at the stage of the path.  With reference to the final result, it acts as a cause to achieving the state of the Enjoyment Body in the Paradise Below No Other.

rows.acip: TSAR CHEN GYIS, YID 'ONG RGYAL YUM + RTZE DGAS ROL BAR SHOG ,CES GSUNGS TE, PHYI NANG GSANG BA'I RNAL 'BYOR MA'I RANG ZHAL MTHONG BA'I SMON LAM YIN LA, DE YANG SNGAGS SKYES LHAN SKYES PHO NYA'I TSOGS, ZHES GSUNGS PA LTAR, BUD MED LAM THUN MONG BAS RGYUD SBYANGS PA BSKYED RIM GYI RTOGS PA SNE ZIN SKYES PA SNGAGS SKYES DANG, YUL NYER BZHI'I ZHING SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA DANG, 'OG MIN LHAN SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA 'DU BA STE MJAL BAR SHOG CES PA DANG,
rows.wylie: tshar chen gyis, yid 'ong rgyal yum + rtse dgas rol bar shog ,ces gsungs te, phyi nang gsang ba'i rnal 'byor ma'i rang zhal mthong ba'i smon lam yin la, de yang sngags skyes lhan skyes pho nya'i tshogs, zhes gsungs pa ltar, bud med lam thun mong bas rgyud sbyangs pa bskyed rim gyi rtogs pa sne zin skyes pa sngags skyes dang, yul nyer bzhi'i zhing skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma dang, 'og min lhan skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma 'du ba ste mjal bar shog ces pa dang
rows.english: Now Tsarchen has those lines that go, "May I laugh and play...in the one who steals my heart."   This is a prayer for seeing the face of the outer, inner, and secret forms of the Angel. Remember too the lines that talk about "A crowd of messengers...born of the secret word, the simultaneous."  Messengers "born of the secret word" are women who have been trained in the shared path, and who have a good foundation in realizations of the creation stage.  Messenger "born of holy places" are women who come from the 24 holy places.  Messengers "born of the simultaneous" are women who are living in the Heaven Below No Other.  And so what Master Tsarchen is praying for here is that these Messengers can gather together, and that He meets them.

rows.acip: YANG SKABS SKABS SU RNAL 'BYOR MA DE DAG KYANG 'OG MIN NA BZHUGS PA'I RNAL 'BYOR MA DANG BDE CHEN 'KHOR LO'I YUM BZHI, PHYI'I YUL NYER BZHI DANG DUR KHROD BRGYAD SOGS NA DA LTA DNGOS SU BZHUGS PA'I DPA' BO MKHA' 'GRO DANG GNYIS SU MED PA'I RNAL 'BYOR MA DE DANG DE DNGOS YIN SNYAM PA STE BSAM BLO GNYIS DGOS,
rows.wylie: yang skabs skabs su rnal 'byor ma de dag kyang 'og min na bzhugs pa'i rnal 'byor ma dang bde chen 'khor lo'i yum bzhi, phyi'i yul nyer bzhi dang dur khrod brgyad sogs na da lta dngos su bzhugs pa'i dpa' bo mkha' 'gro dang gnyis su med pa'i rnal 'byor ma de dang de dngos yin snyam pa ste bsam blo gnyis dgos
rows.english: From time to time though in the meditation you should also reflect on how each Angel is in truth this or that Angel who already existed; that they are entirely indivisible from the Holy Angel and the four Wives of the Wheel of Great Bliss who even now reside in the Heaven Below No Other, and the various Warriors and Angels who are present in the twenty-four sacred places and the eight burial grounds of the outer world.  Thus there are two states of mind you must retain.

rows.acip: SKABS SKABS SU RANG GI GNAS KYANG 'OG MIN DANG YUL NYER BZHI SOGS DNGOS YIN SNYAM PA DANG , KHA t+V'A GA'I MTSON DON RNAMS SHES PAR BYAS NAS DE NYID LA HE RU KA'I RTEN DANG BRTEN PA'I DKYIL 'KHOR GYI GNAD RNAMS KYANG TSANG BAR MOS PA GAL CHE,
rows.wylie: skabs skabs su rang gi gnas kyang 'og min dang yul nyer bzhi sogs dngos yin snyam pa dang , kha T+vA ga'i mtshon don rnams shes par byas nas de nyid la he ru ka'i rten dang brten pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi gnad rnams kyang tshang bar mos pa gal che
rows.english: Then and again in the meditation as well it is very important for you to think to yourself how your own place is actually the Heaven Below No Other, or the twenty-four sacred lands, or the like.  Learn all the symbolism too of the khatvanga staff, and then keep a strong feeling of how all the essential elements of the entire secret world of Heruka, both the place and the beings that stay there, are all complete in this single object.

rows.acip: YANG YI GE GSUM GYIS PHO NYA GSUM MTSON PA NI, RANG RNAL 'BYOR MAR BSGOMS PA DANG SEMS CAN THAMS CAD RNAL 'BYOR MAR GYUR PA NI SNGAGS SKYES KYI PHO NYA, YUL NYER BZHI'I RNAL 'BYOR MA NI ZHING SKYES KYI PHO NYA, 'OG MIN NA ZHUGS PA NI, LHAN SKYES KYI PHO NYA STE DE THAMS CAD GCIG TU BSRE BA LA PHO NYA GSUM BSRE ZHES GSUNGS,
rows.wylie: yang yi ge gsum gyis pho nya gsum mtshon pa ni, rang rnal 'byor mar bsgoms pa dang sems can thams cad rnal 'byor mar gyur pa ni sngags skyes kyi pho nya, yul nyer bzhi'i rnal 'byor ma ni zhing skyes kyi pho nya, 'og min na zhugs pa ni, lhan skyes kyi pho nya ste de thams cad gcig tu bsre ba la pho nya gsum bsre zhes gsungs
rows.english: You can also say that the three letters represent the three different kinds of Messengers.  The Angel that I am visualizing myself as, and the Angels represented by all the suffering beings who transformed into Her--are Messengers born of the secret word.  The Angels who live in the 24 sacred sites are the Messengers born of the holy places.  The Angels who live in the Heaven Below No Other then are the Messengers born of the simultaneous.  And when They all mix together as one here then we call it the �fusion of the three Messengers.�

rows.acip: YUL NYER BZHI'I DPA' MO RNAMS ZHING SKYES TE PHO NYA 'BRING , 'OG MIN NA BZHUGS PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA PHO NYA RAB STE PHYI'I PHO NYA GSUM DANG ,
rows.wylie: yul nyer bzhi'i dpa' mo rnams zhing skyes te pho nya 'bring , 'og min na bzhugs pa'i lhan skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma pho nya rab ste phyi'i pho nya gsum dang
rows.english: The woman Warriors of the twenty-four sacred lands are the Messengers we say are "born of holy places," and these are the middling Messengers.  The Holy Angels who reside in the Heaven Below No Other are those we call "born of the simultaneous," and they are the higher Messenger.  These then are the three outer Messengers.

rows.acip: BDAG BSKYED RKYANG PA'I SKABS TSOGS 'BUL NA 'OG MIN MA'I GONG DANG, BDAG 'JUG SKABS 'OG TU BYED PA'I KHYAD PAR YOD,
rows.wylie: bdag bskyed rkyang pa'i skabs tshogs 'bul na 'og min ma'i gong dang, bdag 'jug skabs 'og tu byed pa'i khyad par yod
rows.english: There is a distinction here that you should be aware of.  If you plan to make the offering of the Gathering on an occasion when all you are doing is the practice of turning yourself into the Angel, then you should do so before the section on the Heaven Below No Other.  Whenever you are taking yourself in though, you should make this offering after that section.

rows.acip: 'DI KHRID KYI TSE NYIN STAR GSAR PA BSHAMS TE 'BREL GTOR GYI 'OG MIN MA'I DUS SU 'BUL, MTSAMS KYI SKABS 'OG MIN MA'I GTOR MA 'DI NYIN RE BZHIN GSAR BRJE MI DGOS PAR GTOR SGAM DU BSHAMS PAS CHOG ,
rows.wylie: 'di khrid kyi tshe nyin star gsar pa bshams te 'brel gtor gyi 'og min ma'i dus su 'bul, mtshams kyi skabs 'og min ma'i gtor ma 'di nyin re bzhin gsar brje mi dgos par gtor sgam du bshams pas chog
rows.english: During periods when a teaching is being delivered on this practice, you should make a new torma of this kind each day, and offer it up during the part of ceremony for the torma of relationship in the section about the Heaven Below No Other.  When you are staying in retreat, you need not replace this torma of the Heaven Below No Other with a new one each day; it is permissible to place it in a special cabinet which protects the torma.

rows.acip: DE MDUN RANG GI G-YON NAS 'GO BRTZAMS PA'I BDAG BSKYED KYI CHU GNYIS NYER SPYOD TSAR GCIG LOGS SHIG TU 'OG MIN MA'I DMAR ZLUM SKED PAR PAD 'DAB BZHIS BSKOR BA, BRANG RGYAN LNGA KHRAM, RTZE RGYAN NYI ZLA N'A DA, PHYAG BZHES DPE RIS TSAD LDAN MANG POR YANG 'DI LTAR BYUNG,
rows.wylie: de mdun rang gi g-yon nas 'go brtsams pa'i bdag bskyed kyi chu gnyis nyer spyod tshar gcig logs shig tu 'og min ma'i dmar zlum sked par pad 'dab bzhis bskor ba, brang rgyan lnga khram, rtse rgyan nyi zla nA da, phyag bzhes dpe ris tshad ldan mang por yang 'di ltar byung
rows.english: Placed before these goes yet another line of offering bowls, these starting from our left.  These are offered to ourselves as the Angel, and again consist of two waters followed by the objects of the senses.  Off to one side here we place the Torma for the Lady of the Heaven Below No Other.  It is red, and conical in shape.  Four lotus petals circle it at the midpoint, and again at the top center it has the five-part ornamentation, along with the additional top adornment, sun, crescent, and nada.  You see it this way in a lot of authentic drawings of the tradition.

rows.acip: TSES BCU BSDUS PA NI, BDAG BSKYED KYI, DNGOS GRUB MA LUS PA STZAL DU GSOL, ZHES PA'I MJUG TU TSOGS 'KHOR BYA ZHING, TSOGS LHAG 'OG MIN MA'I MJUG TU BTON PA LAS GZHAN TSANG MA BDAG BSKYED GZHUNG LTAR BYED PA YIN NO,,
rows.wylie: tshes bcu bsdus pa ni, bdag bskyed kyi, dngos grub ma lus pa stsal du gsol, zhes pa'i mjug tu tshogs 'khor bya zhing, tshogs lhag 'og min ma'i mjug tu bton pa las gzhan tshang ma bdag bskyed gzhung ltar byed pa yin no
rows.english: For an abbreviated version of the Offering of the Tenth, follow the text for turning yourself into Her, up to the point that includes the words, "Grant us every one of our goals."  The Circle of Gathering should come then right after that, and the offering of the remainders of the gathering should be read out after the section dedicated to the Lady of the Heaven Below No Other.  All the rest follows the normal order of the text of the ritual for becoming Her.

rows.acip: PHYI ROL 'OG MIN NA BZHUGS PA NI LHAN SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA STE PHYI'I RNAL 'BYOR MA RAB, 'DZAM BU GLING GI YUL NYER BZHI SOGS NA BZHUGS PA NI ZHING SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA STE 'BRING, LAM MTHUN MONG DANG MTHUN MONG MIN PA LA RIM GYIS SBYANGS PAS BSKYED RIM GYI RTOGS PA SNE ZIN SKYES PA YAN CHAD NI SNGAGS SKYES KYI RNAL 'BYOR MA STE THA MA YIN LA,
rows.wylie: phyi rol 'og min na bzhugs pa ni lhan skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma ste phyi'i rnal 'byor ma rab, 'dzam bu gling gi yul nyer bzhi sogs na bzhugs pa ni zhing skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma ste 'bring, lam mthun mong dang mthun mong min pa la rim gyis sbyangs pas bskyed rim gyi rtogs pa sne zin skyes pa yan chad ni sngags skyes kyi rnal 'byor ma ste tha ma yin la
rows.english: Then outside, staying in the Heaven Below No Other, is the spontaneous Diamond Angel--this is the highest form of the outer Angel.  Living in the 24 sacred lands of Earth and the like are the Angels born of holy places--these are the medium type of outer Angel. And one who has at the very least had realizations of the main points of the stage of creation, by becoming adept in the steps of both the shared and unique paths, is an Angel born of the secret word--this is the lowest kind of outer Angel.

rows.acip: PHYI'I PHO NYA RAB NI, 'OG MIN NA BZHUGS PA'I LHAN SKYES KYI RGYAL YUM RDO RJE RNAL 'BYOR MA DANG, 'BRING YUL NYER BZHIN BZHUGS PA'I RAB GTUM MA SOGS ZHING SKYES KYI d'A KI MA,

rows.english: The highest outer messenger is the simultaneous Mother of the Victors, the Angel of Diamond, who resides in the Heaven Below No Other.  The medium outer messengers are the Angels who are "born of holy places": this refers to those--like the Lady of Horrible Wrath--who reside in the 24 sacred lands.

rows.english: Each of Them has At the tip of Their head A letter om; At Their throat A letter ah; And at Their eminent heart A letter hung. From all these letters Fly our rays of light In the form of hooks. rows.english: The body of enjoyment is also being called a "Land of Reality," as are certain specific locations such as the Heaven Below No Other.  And the light rays are--within a single instant--beckoning, from any one or more of these three Lands, Beings of Wisdom who have the same appearance as the holy beings we have been visualizing.  Which is to say, They are in the form either of the body of enjoyment or of the emanation body, each with Their own retinue.

rows.english: The mind is the main thing; and to show this, the following explanation appears in the scripture: The world, in the form of those who live in it, finds its very being through the power of the karma they have collected with their minds, and through the bad thoughts in their minds. This refers to everything up to the farthest reaches of the world, from the great disc of wind that underpins our planet up to the highest temporary heaven, the one named "Below No Other."
